title: The Great Plagiarism
review:
James Cameron, has he lost his inspiration? I believe he did! I respect most of his previous works "Terminator 1 & 2", "The Abyss" even "True Lies" is wonderful. He used to be such an avant-gardist...

But I must say that I was nearly offended when I saw "Avatar". He said on an interview (TF1 French Television) that it took them 3 years to create this movies and its world... Well it is a plagiarism, let me explain:

1. The scenario is basically the one from "Pocahontas".

2. The Shipsare exactly as in the video game "Halo".

3. The Names are from a french comic book "Sillage".

4. The Fauna and Flora are more than inspired by Miyazaki's work...

5. And the robots are exactly the same as in the Matrix!

There is no surprise element in the movie what's so ever if you've seen "Pocahontas". And most of all there is no consistency in the world, animals destroys their environment, humans dress the same way as now in the future etc.

The positive point is that the 3D and the visual effects are wonderful. And I guess for most of the people this must be the main criteria for a good movie...

title: All visuals and nothing else.
review:
If you're someone who enjoys movies made by Tim Burton, which are heavier on atmosphere and visuals than actual story, this movie is for you. If your someone who enjoys a good story with good acting and writing, than don't even bother watching this.

This movie is mediocre to the last degree. The acting is extraordinarily bad, and the writing is bland. This is an extremely overrated motion picture using great visuals and picture to make money, a sad example of what's happened to film, it's no longer to entertain, but it seems it's more of a contest of who can make more money. Do not watch.

title: Vastly overrated
review:
Firstly to say that I've only seen the 2D version.

For such a high profile film that had garnered so many favourable views I have to say this must be the worst (high profile film) I have ever seen.

I had not read the database before viewing the film but recalled the reviews on it's release. The first thing one has to say is the plot, as other have mentioned, is a direct lift from Dances With Wolves.

To quote Edmund Blackadder 'it was as predictable as a predictable thing can be predicted', something I was quite (un)happily doing throughout the film. It isn't even so bad it's good - although there a couple of unintentionally funny scenes (well I laughed).

The actors do the best they can with a very average script with Steven Lang as the main hate character in a destroy everything sort of way, played so over the top he could be a pantomime villain. It's not his fault of course, James Cameron directed him! The CG graphics/special effects look OK but gave me no real sense of warmth to the characters, I didn't find then innovative just a bit soulless.

If 2 and a half hours of overly blue CGI/Special effects is your thing OK but I found it a total waste of the time.

title: The Unintended Consequences of This ...Film
review:
Well here we are, more than a year after the general release of "Avatar". Most of the hype has finally dissipated, exposing it to be a wasteland of ultra-liberal elitist fantasy fueled by some of the most pernicious corporate greed. Cameron would call it "film promotion". Let's call it what it really is: propaganda. An example of Madison Avenue manipulation at its worst. Marketing research - not to discover what audiences (a.k.a target market) need or want - but to ascertain their weaknesses and exploit them. No need to assess this film's shortcomings - most have been adroitly expressed on this site and elsewhere. At this point, I'd like to consider the possible re-purposing of this cinematic Edsel. Is it possible to use this film to make Avatar anti-toxin?

Millions of minions worldwide have drunk this hemlock and passed it to others, saying "Drink this - you'll be superior". The promise is as sophomorically volatile as the drink itself. There's never been a shortage of vapid impostors of spiritual truth gift-wrapped in gold foil. Maybe, this time, Avatar's industrial-scale superficiality has finally helped pop culture's implosion to reach critical mass. I cite the many reactions (no pun intended) on this very site as support for this hypothesis. There's witnesses a-plenty to this film's naked arrogance and, perhaps more importantly, realization that an attempt was being made to bilk and corrupt them with a mixture of sweet, salty, and sour distractions. Read these analyses. They're not simply whining about being cool or not enough skin or more blood. They recognize that the film is, at its core, a total VACUUM. After being told of its wonders, it's not simply inadequate - it is nothing at all. Many are realizing that not only was this a banal waste of effort, but it is built and based upon a ziggerat of nothingness. These victims of Avatar are awakening from being tranquilized - and it's not pleasant to realize you've been swindled while you were incapacitated. Powerful antidote is illumination...powerful antidote.

Thank you, Avatar. You probably never realized how effective a dispersant you are against the current trend of plot less, character- devoid, dialogue-deprived, humor-starved, anti-creativity films and theatre. Keep up the bad work.

title: EPIC it most certainly is NOT!!!!!!!!!!
review:
The irony of having to tick the may contain spoilers box is rife; and certainly not lost on me. For anyone else that was genuinely blown away by this film please watch something else, anything else! "Mr Bean" for instance ,god even an episode of "Days of our lives" will suffice. Anything in which to have a reference point and obviously it doesn't need to be good! Firstly this film only warranted a 5/10 purely on the technical prowess of WETA studios(the magicians behind "Lord of the Rings"), who are 100% responsible for this films success. This film is "Fern Gully" right down to the last detail. James Cameron should be SUED!!!!!Certainly not revered by what at best are simply ill informed people and at worst are the most ignorant sheltered troglodytes ever to have existed (Darwin would have been so happy, if only you presented yourselves a little earlier; and I seriously doubt that the majority of you will even get the reference. Hence why this film has such a high rating.) Now I absolutely accept other comparisons that people have drawn "Dances with Wolves"etc. But this film IS "Fern Gully"! Lets begin. A boy without purpose just doing whatever is suggested takes a job in a forest (Pandora, such an original name) spray painting red X's on trees to signify there impending harvest. He comes close to one of the natives (i.e. the Nav'i),in this case a Fern Gully fairy, and recognizing her only as a bug getting in the way of his job ,he tries to kill her. The fairy reacts by shrinking the human boy to the size of a fairy. He runs , he plays ,he acts like a 2 year old and ,yes, attracts some predatory organisms nearly getting everyone killed. Oh how the fairy's are both fascinated and fearful of this new addition to there colony. Never fear though because the female fairy, who first shrunk the boy, takes him on a journey of self discovery. He learns how everything is connected i.e. he carves a love heart in a tree professing his adoration for the girl fairy which she reacts to in utter horror. "Can't you feel it's pain!" and so on and so on. Through out this "journey" we see the wonders of a neon forest which lights up at night, pretty floating organisms and, yes, even a scene where they frolic about as the earth lights up with their touch. Now this girl fairy is the spiritual successor to the fairy colony(Any of this sounding familiar at this point).Now enter the lead male fairy who is to be married off to the female spiritual successor fairy and become the new "chief" leader of the colony( please tell me this is starting to sound familiar). Who at first has nothing but contempt for this outsider but soon they come to respect one another as they fight together to save their home blah, blah, and another exhausted blah! Now this is where the similarities just get ridiculous. The evil impending corporates , which are represented by an evil smog and a large yellow harvesting machine (yes that was not a typo a large yellow harvesting machine! can't imagine where iv'e seen that before?Lol.) This machine is getting closer and closer to the sacred tree (yes a giant tree in which the fairy's all live and is their most referred and sacred landmark. Why does that sound so familiar?Lol). The newly introduced human, now the size of a fairy and living amongst the colony, is now revealed to have been in league with the evil corporate harvesters.At this point the lead female fairy and the human boy are, of course, in love. We laugh, we cry and all that blah! He ultimately comes back to help in the fight and prove his love and loyalty utilizing his knowledge of human machines and riding (now wait for it) "Batty" the largest untamable flying creature in "Fern Gully". All the rest fly on standard size beetles once they have earn't the right in an initiation, of course! now at this point in "Avatar" the Freudian in me was wetting it's self. He has the biggest "one" oh how that must make him the alpha male?! The spiritual elder and current chief sacrifice themselves to save the younger fairies and their sacred "big tree". The young spiritual successor fairy now the lead spiritual fairy draws all her strength and calls on all the creatures of fern gully to aid in the fight. The human boy uses his "human intellect" to shut down the big yellow harvester and puts an end to the evil black smog. Not before ,however, much damage is done to there home. Please tell me that someone out there at this point sees "some" similarities? Their have been 2 "Fern Gully" sequels I wonder if they too will be plagiarized by the "talented" James Cameron.

Now I could, of course, go on; further breaking down the similarities. Showing in more detail how this symbolizes that etc. But for those who are fans ,I doubt it will matter, and for the rest of us ,well lets face it, we're smart enough to figure it out.

Normally this would not bother me but after hearing endless praise for this film and reading quotes from other IMDb critics ,such as "Not since "Schindlers list" have I been so moved by a film" etc, I felt I had to say something. I hope that someone else out there will read this and realize they are not alone. It would seem we suffer from "have a measurable I.Q syndrome!" it's a condition I'm happy to have. Even if it means I can't enjoy "al da prutty pictas"!

"UNOBTANIUM" That really should have been enough.

title: What a shame...
review:
Like most people, I was extremely excited to see this, especially in 3D and Imax. Once the movie ended, I looked around at my fellow movie-goers, who were all absolutely blown away, and I thought: "Did I miss something?" Apparently I did not. It was an absolute disappointment.

Superficially it is beautiful. Pandora is a wonderful world, with nice special effects and whatnot. I didn't feel that it was revolutionary; we've seen brilliant imaginations at work before that I've found far more revolutionary (i.e. anything by Miyazaki) But I will still give it some credit for the hard work on making this planet look like paradise.

OK, what went wrong? Basically everything else. The story had an excellent premise, but took every wrong turn leading to so many things we've seen before. One third of the way into the film you can call what will happen, who it will happen to, and what the end will be. It's really a shame, this could have been phenomenal with a good script. But for some reason, James Cameron thought crap for a story would be nice for a thick layer of visual effects disguise.

I see the appeal, but in today's world all we seem to care about are special effects. I guess it's taken over the most crucial part of cinema, the plot.

title: forgettable flick, might be state of the art right now effects-wise, but ridiculously weak plot
review:
i watched this yesterday and i was really disappointed, i cannot see what people see in this movie. the story makes no sense at all, all the characters are really clichéd, and the whole movie is ridiculously predictable.

especially the plot element with the marine being in a wheelchair feels really forced, seeing some guy in a wheelchair in a spaceship between walking mecha-robots felt unreal, even more unreal than the sigourney weaver character smoking inside a tech lab 150 years in the future...

as for the visuals, they might be the best effects to date, but the world of pandora still doesn't look real. it has a computer-gamish look on it, and since the whole storyline is like something someone wrote down in 10 minutes for a computer game, i couldn't help but feeling like i was watching some game trailer.

title: Avatar, great date film
review:
It's got something for everyone, romanticized compassion with love for "Mother Earth" for the gals, and lots of mechanical high-tech blow-ups, blow-outs....for the guys. It isn't too mushy and it doesn't beat you over the head with PC....it's great fun for everyone. Just go for the sheer joy of the paintings....and the special effect worlds...gorgeous. title: Very blah
review:

title: Dances with Smurfs in Ferngully
review:
In Avatar, a bunch of marines in a big spacecraft (with a rotating segment - Aliens) are woken from hyper-sleep (Alien) and drop shipped to a new planet (Aliens) in a vehicle with a snub-nosed cockpit (Aliens). The planet is inhabited by ten-foot tall blue aliens (Battlefield Earth) who worship a big tree (Pochahontas) One of the marines is able to mix in with the natives (Ferngully) and comes to love them. The native culture glows as does their forest with a conveniently visible energy religion (Tron). Something meaningful is conveyed with the phrase "I SEE you!" (Joy Luck Club). In the end there is a war featuring man-shaped robot-exoskeletons (Mars Attacks, Transformers, Star Wars, Aliens, District 9, MIB, Robocop, Terminator). And a Latina Marine sacrifices herself (Aliens).

What surprising about Avatar is how shamelessly derivative it is, while 20-year olds ignorant of older movies tell you it's the most original, most important thing since glow-in-the-dark bread. I hope to never see another movie with the exoskeleton idea again. Because 20 years later, films have thoroughly exhausted the concept. There is some good stuff in Avatar. Chief among it, is a subversive viewer-identity concept that has you rooting against your own species/planet. It's perfectly appropriate that Cameron sees through the Iraq war and the moral bankruptcy of both corporations and the Right; but he dares to say five thousand marines with tunnel-vision being led by a hot-head who's never created anything, are NOT the pride of the nation. And he's right. It's very strange to be delighted when the humans finally get decimated. A strange moment to witness... and it's brought to you by the growing revulsion people feel for a misused army and for evil corporations in general, and the sickening cross-pollination of the two.

Two gigantic moral quandaries are never even addressed: Isn't it unethical to make living things that have no life until a person avatars them? And the marine is still selling out the natives waaaaaay after he's come to admire them ??? The movie is not really science fiction... it is fantasy, which is not really my cup of Q'thar. If you've seen one Native American documentary and two National Geographic specials, you've seen these ideas before. (Why do I keep buying the 3-D glasses? In every 3-D movie, the effect is interesting for exactly ten minutes.)

title: Hard to take seriously despite interesting imagery
review:
All I have to say is no amount of creative digital imagery can make up for the lack of overall good writing and/or acting in this film.

For a film with serious messages, it was hard to take seriously with the cartoonish special effects. Giant smurfs with a vendetta against humanity taken straight from the Greenpeace movement don't particularly help with that particular political agenda.

While I admired the good digital scenery effects, I think the characters needed a lot more production work before the film's final release. None of that could have made up for how ridiculous the character of Colonel Miles Quaritch was played out, or the emotionally unmoving aspects of the relationship between Jake Sully and Neytiri. In the end, I found myself rooting for the military as they chopped down the "home tree" and laughing as the giant smurfs sat around another tree, singing to invoke Jake Sully into his smurf body.

The entire plot was extremely predictable. Interesting idea for a film, but an epic failure in following through with the concept for this audience member. The critics must have been paid a lot to let this one past their critical radar.

title: Incredible visuals, surprisingly lame movie
review:
Yes, the visuals in Avatar are awesome. I saw it in 3-D and agree that it looks amazing.

Unfortunately, it still isn't that great. In fact, it's the most over-hyped and overrated movie of the year. Anyone wanting more than special effects (intelligence? god forbid) is not going to have fun at this movie. I suspect that the more movies you've seen, the less Avatar will impress you. Of course, even the critics (inexplicably) think this is the greatest thing since canned spam, so perhaps I'm wrong.

The biggest problem with Avatar is that its story is mind-numbingly generic, mediocre, unoriginal, predictable pap. It's Ferngully with better special effects. There weren't any twists or surprises here to engage or interest me in the slightest, which made for a dull and sometimes extremely boring film. The film's fans claim that "every story has already been told" and therefore we shouldn't criticize it. But that's nonsense. If no new film ever had any suspense, people would quickly stop watching them.

And then there's the running time. At 80 minutes, Avatar might have been tolerable. At 162, it's an endurance test. Especially with the lame characters and recycled story.

Honestly, I don't think I could even sit through this bore a second time.

title: Best Film Experience I've had, probably ever.

Seen it in 3D, if you get the chance to see it in 3D, do so, YOU WILL NOT BE DISAPPOINTED!

BREATHTAKING!

title: Going Native: AVATARA visual feast: fantastic film...SPOILERS
review:
Well, after months of waiting ,i finally got to see Avatar, a film all about going native... with a vengeance. My worst fears, from the trailer: hackneyed dialogue, didn't materialise, and tho the script was excellent, it was the actors who brought it and Pandora to life. Subtle, tender, sweet, brutal, menacing:cameron doesn't do things by halves. The tenderness of the two leads is as convincing as the initial menace of the na'vi and the growing menace of the humans. Worthington and Saldana are splendid as the two leads...Worthinton making his slow and painful transition from human to navi credible by digging into his character and finding the heart. The direction, script and running time allow space for this transformation...

NO: Its not necessary to have a completely new idea...but it is important to make it come alive. In this Cameron and his crew have succeeded...much of this is due to the SFX teams and the actors. Saldana may have been as much of a chance for Cameron as Worthinton(who made me think of Russell Crowe), being little known, and having #150,000,000 riding on her slender form but she gives life and passion to elven Neytiri: as the princess, teacher friend and lover to the initially wild Jake: going from a wish to kill, contempt slowly shedding these as she recognises Jakes worth(pun!) and teaches him the ways of her people. The spine of the film is his transformation, which is one of the highlights. Lang as Qaritch, is also terrific as the brutal Qaritch, with his single vision, and dark alter-teacher to Jake...Marked like Ahab, has only made his character the more ominous..he's like a bomb waiting to go off. Sigoruney Weaver is terrific as the tough principled scientist, who stands up to the corporate mercenaries. I liked the idea where jakes 'emptiness' was used to his advantage over the scientists in bridging the gulf between human and Navi. Interesting irony, this scene echoes the tea pouring scene in that other fabulous epic: 2012. Notable feature of the film is nits use of parallels: esp the robot transports who counterparts to the Avatars: the mechanical/scientific vs the natural/mystical embody the confrontation we see in our world. Ironical. The world itself is loving rendered: almost it looks as if cameron has been to pandora and filmed live. But we can see where much of the money went! From the great trees, to the luminous seedpods, flying beasts and snarling dog things, floating mountains and calling waterfalls the world is rendered in marvelous detail. Beautiful and dangerous. Avatar is the furthest anyone has gone in rendering alien worlds in mainstream life action films...only European animation (Fantastic Planet) has gone further.

And tho the people are blue, there's not a smurf in sight...

title: Top Film if a little predictable
review:
Saw this in 3D today - has my thumbs up! The 3D works (even with my vision) and the story, although predictable (I'd figured out the ending by about 20 minutes into the film) was nonetheless very enjoyable and touched me deeply in several scenes.

Actually, the film reminded me a lot of two SF stories: Call me Joe by Poul Anderson, and Hothouse by Brian Aldiss. Anyway, the themes are not new, but what is new is the totality of the treatment. Almost all of the action takes place in an alien environment with the Narvi - all of which is computer generated. There is live action footage and characters spliced into this as well, and it is absolutely seamless. Within 10 minutes I was immersed into the environment, and wishing it really existed!

With a lot of films of this ilk the plot is a bit simplistic. We don't know much about the corporation exploiting the planet, but we can guess that this is either the same one seen in the Aliens films, or one very similar in operation. Really though the situation mirrors a number of colonial and post-colonial situations in recent history, where local and indigenous populations lost out to overseas interest in their resources.

No doubt about who the "bad guys" are and this is pretty clear from the trailer. It takes time but you learn about the Narvi over the course of the film and come to understand their culture and religion - a religion that seems to be based on a "real goddess" as well. But it's also clear that ultimately the good guys will win, and that the main character will, well you'll see. Suffice it to say that what happens is telegraphed well before it occurs.

But even with its predictability, I loved this film. I shall have to see it again, without the 3D,to see if that makes a difference.

title: I love Pandorra
review:
Finally Avatar has arrived.I was one of the thousands who bought tickets in advance to avoid disappointment.Yes the movie was great.Very nice story,excellent graphics and a nice message too.

However,Avatar too has some not-so-nice-things to list.Cameron has largely depended on the technology used and graphics to make the movie work.In fact the story seems to be tailor-made to exploit the groundbreaking technology.But to me the graphics just seemed to be similar to other sci-fi movies such as star trek,star wars(revenge of the sith) and lotr.In fact i enjoyed Star Trek(2009) more because i went to star trek with no hype and JJ Abrams was no Cameron to build much hype.

secondly for most parts the movie was just like a first-person-shooter game centering the lead avatar.The occasional zooming in effects reminded me games such as Crysis and Call-of-duty but the effects were nice.and the movie was mostly predictable with the good guys winning at the climax.The build up to the conflict and the hero's rise were all clichéd.

Pandorra was definitely worth a visit and its spectacular lifeforms are mind-blowing but James Cameron definitely could have thought better for this 12 years wait.his earlier movies such as Titanic,Terminator 2 and alien were much much better.They were more engrossing,thrilling and original.Cameron could have jut a made a movie with real people i the real world.Doubt this movie can justify his portfolio.

Apart from the bad thing Avatar definitely has its share of commendable stuff.As per most reviews the soundtrack of this movie was wonderful and i am going to watch this movie again just for that.But this time in 2d as found the 3d distracting.The emotional scenes between neytiri and jake sully's avatar were nice.James Cameron is a master in writing romantic scenes.

Avatar is worth the watch but its just another sci-fi movie and its definitely not going to dethrone Titanic.Lets see how Tin Tin(Spielberg) and Inception(Christopher Nolan) fare in 2010

title: Stunning on a technical level, poor on plot and script.
review:
Jake Sully arrives on the planet Pandora to take the place of his dead brother in using a creature known as an 'Avatar' to try and move the native people from their home, so humans can mine for a rock that's under it. However, as Sully spends more time with the Na'vi, he finds his loyalty tested....

James Cameron spent around 14 years getting the technology he needed to film this movie. Filming the actors using motion capture technology, then using CGI to replace the actors on screen. It was used for characters such as Gollum in The Lord Of The Rings trilogy, and on movies such as Beowulf, however this is without doubt the best use of the technology in a movie so far. The CGI is stunning, creating an imaginative world and also some impressive alien creatures.

It's always hard to judge performances when done using motion capture, but I'd have to say on the whole the cast are pretty good, the stand-out being Stephen Lang as Col. Quaritch. Sam Worthington as Sully is also very impressive in the lead role.

Cameron, as he has shown in the past stages some very impressive action sequences in the last part of the movie, but also directs the quieter moments very well to.

However....

First of all, for all the time spent on the technology side, Cameron should have spent more time on the story and script. The plot line is very predictable, and some of the dialogue is very poor. Perhaps next movie, he should bring in a scriptwriter to help out.

The 3-D side of the movie, while impressive wasn't the immersive experience I was expecting. In fact, I don't think the movie actually benefits being in 3-D at all. I'm one of those waiting to be convinced that 3-D is the big thing everyone thinks it will be, and nothing in Avatar on that side convinces me.

As I said the CGI is very impressive indeed, but as good as it is, and as good as the action scenes are done, there is no actual tension or excitement. Unlike movies of the past, where you had stunt-men doing actual stunts, the reliance on CGI in modern movies has taken that away, resulting in no sense of dread or risk during the action parts. Avatar isn't the first movie to suffer for this, but it is becoming more and more apparent in movies these days and I wish it would stop.

Another flaw with the CGI is that, some of the emotional aspects of the movie are lost. While it is without doubt the best movie yet of it's kind, the technology still, as yet can't get the emotional side of the performances quite right. It is close, but until they can solve this flaw you won't feel for the characters and their story.

The film is also far too long. The central section of the movie goes on and on, and slows everything down. I'm understand why it's there, to show Sully falling for the Na'vi culture, and also in love, but it just feels baggy.

There is no denying that James Cameron has created a movie that looks fantastic. But I wish he'd spent as much time on the script as he had on the technology side. If he had, he might have made a movie that is the so-called 'game changer' of the movie industry that Avatar is claimed to be (though to be fair, I don't think Cameron has said this himself). Instead, he has only made a movie that looks good, but nothing more.

A pity.

title: Avatar - the disappointing Cameron film
review:
Ladies and gentlemen, put your hands together for the most well-done CGI hand in hand with the most disappointed movie of the year - yes, put your hands together for Avatar.

No, no - don't get me wrong. The movie's not bad. But the script is horribly weak! I don't know if this has anything to do with the fact that I was watching a dubbed version, but the dialogues were disappointing enough. Cameron has come up with the most convincing CGI production, but, I wonder why, he only relies on the CGI? Why didn't he work more on the story and, specially the script? The direction is very slow at times, and tends to get irritating. The predictability of the movie is the worst part. We're tired of the some-stroke-of-luck last- minute-life-saving moments of the lead roles. Let them DIE man!

Go watch Avatar for the deliciously sweet eye-candy, but if you're hoping for something big, then you might as well skip it.

title: beautiful but a tad infantile and predictable story
review: Unfortunately Cameron looks down to the public and offers us a story so full of clichés and of a simplified view of the world, people and the Universe in general, that it is truly condescending. Neither he nor the studio behind him respect their audience. And after they sunk a reported 400 or so million in the project who can blame them? They need to recoup at least most of this money, and they do it by trying to appeal to as broad an audience as possible. I think Jim Schembri from The Age sums it up very well: "There's no argument that, as a showcase for the immersive potential of 3D visual effects technology, James Cameron's sci-fi epic Avatar is an unqualified triumph. But as a story designed to engage, enthral and entertain adult audiences for almost three hours, it is a disappointment strewn with weak characters, environmental platitudes and anti-progress clichés. A compulsive envelope-pusher, Cameron invented a pioneering camera system and ground-breaking visual processing techniques for the film, but perhaps he should have spent a little less time obsessing over the technology and a tad more developing the story beyond the compendium of clichés it regrettably is." My vote is 10 + 4/ 2 = 7.

title: God, I HATED James Cameron's Avatar, the most overrated film of 2009, and by far his weakest film!
review:
I hated Avatar.

Those three words are more true than anything else I can think of right now. With one of the biggest film budgets in history, and with his first film since Titanic, James Cameron puts another big budget film back on the big screen.

The visual effects were average, the characters VERY forgettable, the dialog atrocious, the plot very predictable, and the storyline was extremely unoriginal.

Instead of something remotely original, Cameron took elements from Dances With Wolves, the animated films, Ferngully and Pocahontas, The Matrix, and his own Terminator films and combined them into one of the biggest messes ever put on the big screen.

By the end of the film I cared absolutely nothing for any of the characters, the lead is about as dull as the bottom of my shoe, the idiotic "blue monkeys" were irritating, and the evil humans just got more laughable as time went on.

The fact that so many people view this film as good film-making makes me question the intelligence of every person who does so. This isn't good film-making, it's just as bad directing as Michael Bay at his worst. I can guarantee you that if James Cameron's name wasn't attached to this awful film, it would have RAZZIE written all over it. In fact, I think the script and the direction should both get RAZZIE nominations, and I could care less what the fans of this ridiculous film think.

Avatar is not only James Cameron's weakest film, it's also film-making for the lowest common denominator!

title: Ah, what a wonderful piece of.... Discovery Channel documentary
review: I don't want to bash this movie. Trust me, I don't. It truly hurts me more than anything that I have to call this movie nothing more than some of the most gorgeous CGI ever committed to film. They are really mesmerizing and absolutely stunning. The reason I gave this movie a 1/10 however is that visuals(no matter how transcendent in their nature), do not make a movie. They make part of a movie. For this reason the movie feels in my opinion to be rushed, as if they focused completely on the graphics over the story. So basically, this is what the Star Wars prequels would look like if done by James Cameron: All special effects, and very little story and character development. Frankly, Avatar is a very powerful disappointment, and I expect better from James Cameron, who is practically legendary in his skills as a filmmaker.

title: Welcome to 21 century western style ......
review:
Welcome to 21 century western style ...all is missing is a John Wayne avatar ... am so disappointed, oh YES, big time.

CGA and 3-D effects are fabulous, like nothing one this world, but after 60 maybe 90 minutes, the magic is gone and the lack of original storyline is to conspicuous.

I guest they were to much into the magics of new special effects and they just forgot to get at least a decent script.

What is puzzled me is where in the woods they spend 400+ millions $, it's just beyond me, and I know software....! Probably,in the final bill they add the cleaning lady to with like 5000$/day! For 400mil.$ Cameron could almost fix a country like Haiti or East Timor and get a Nobel Price! What a waste of creative energy and money.

title: Painfully unoriginal
review: Avatar was painfully unoriginal. Sure it looks good, but I've seen this same tired worn out story 40 times during my 47 years on this planet. It is too long -- it clock in at 2 1/2 ass-numbing hours-- too boring, and it takes itself way too seriously. Not to mention the fact that there are plot holes big enough to drive a Mack truck through. I would have thought that for $300 million Cameron could have bought an original story. Instead, Avatar offers the same old worn out themes that leftist Hollywood has been cranking out since the communist infiltration back in the late 1940s. The top three reasons why I go to see a movie are ENTERTAINMENT! ENTERTAINMENT!! ENTERTAINMENT!!! Unfortunately, despite all of it's pretty bells & whistles Avatar does not deliver.

title: Very overrated
review:
This movie has great special effects and a cool central sci-fi theme; the concept of an "avatar." 9 or 10 stars for each. But unfortunately the movie lacks any cohesive plot, has cookie-cutter characters and cliché dialog. This lack of originality destroys what should be emotionally charged moments and creates painfully stereotyped/racist portrayals. Also, the beauty of the digital animation is undermined by uninspired cinematography. So 10 stars for animation, but everything else was below average: 3 or 4 stars each for direction, writing, cinematography, plot, etc.

Overall, this is a bad movie which contains one or two precious gems: the avatar concept is wonderful fantasy, and the images are stunning.

title: Visually astounding, flat plat and character
review:
As visually mind-boggling the movie may be - it is a step back in storytelling as well.

Sure, for a blockbuster movie it's a solid experience - but nothing more. The plot and characters are as flat as in a cheap b-movie.

While setting a new standard for a visual experience, this movie is on the level of a cheap kids movie about indians when it comes to the script. The story is a science-fiction conversion of old native Americans stories combined with the worst you would expect of a science- fiction b-movie. Actually the science-fiction elements and characters are quite similar to tarantinos planet terror which was made to look and feel like a b- movie.

The computer-generated world in an realistic 3D look could be so compelling, so near to real life that you could lose yourself in this second reality - but for me - the story was so see-through that you could predict a least the next 15 minutes of the movie at any time.

Cameron uses so many elements of typical native American clichés that this setting can't be understood as alien - it is an alien world, but with indians riding through it, fighting white men with bows and arrows.

This movie lacks a deeper understanding of any kind of scriptwriting - it's a more than just straighforward story with a few quotes from the characters than simply match what you expect them to say. There aren't any twists and turns - and to the intellectual mind - this movie is quite an insult. From it's story it's merely a better children's story.

But as said before the visuals are groundbreaking and are making this movie worthwhile. I found myself just gazing at this amazing scenarios - even if Cameron choose to give wide parts of the world a much too colourful, toy-like appearance.

This movie is a rather entertaining time-killer with amazing visuals. Not more. Not less.

title: Extraordinary? Yes! Revolutionary? No...
review:
Just came from the morning screening of Avatar on opening day in Brisbane...

Let's get the obvious stuff out of the way first. The effects are completely photo real! The 3D is sensational! The Na'vi performances are scarily authentic! But let's not dwell on that because everyone else is gushing on those points. Let's talk about the problems, because they are there...

First, the story. There's nothing really wrong with the story. Jake (Sam Worthington) infiltrates an alien race using his avatar to provide intelligence and to convince them to move as they rest on a valuable mineral deposit. He learns their customs and falls in love with one of them and is forced to choose between honoring his contract or defending his new friends. The story is well structured and well paced - despite running for three hours - but there are no surprises. You know that Jake's loyalty will be challenged and that gun-happy Col Quaritch (Stephen Lang) will declare war on the native tribe. It's great to watch it unfold but I can't help but wish for more suspense in not knowing what would happen...

Second, the performances. Neytiri is a fantastic character and Zoe Saldana plays her perfectly. She is strong and wise, yet vulnerable and feminine. She is also surprisingly hot for a non-human. She is the heart of the film. Stephen Lang provides the balls as Quaritch. He is one tough son of a b*tch in this movie and Lang's great voice and physique really sell that this is a character you don't want to enrage. However, everyone else is only average. Sam Worthington was fine as a leading man and some of his awkward attempts to integrate into the tribe are great, but he's not very engaging on an emotional level. Sigourney Weaver doesn't really do anything to justify her casting - her role could have been played by any middle-aged woman.

Third, the 3D... now for 99.5% of the film, it's beautiful and perfect. But every now and then, objects in the extreme foreground seemed to lose the 3D effect and become the "I'm seeing double" effect you would get if you saw the film without the glasses. That was a little distracting... What was worse was the way we see the world. In wide shots, it's fine because we see the world in wide shots. However, in closeups where the depth of field is shallow, it looks unnatural. I think this is because we don't see the world in a telephoto lens or with such a narrow depth of field. And while the brain is convinced of the 3D effect, you can't get focus on the background and that irritated my eyes a little.

Now this is by no means a bad film. It is a fantastic film. On a cinematic level, the world Cameron presents is so real and so organic that you can't help but get drawn into it. You are convinced that this world exists. For the first time since Jurassic Park, I actually had to pinch myself to remember that those exterior locations are completely computer generated because they didn't just look realistic... they actually were real in my mind.

Lastly, I loved the themes in this film and how he depicts them in the story. I'm no Greenpeace activist, but I believe in generally keeping things natural and whilst I'm not religious, I do consider myself spiritual. James Cameron really impressed me as he deals with nature and spirituality-slash-mysticism in this film and manages to explain it through biology and chemistry rather than implying any sort of holy deity. For that I commend him as other films such as I am Legend have lost points for implying a specific religion when it should have been more generic... after all how do we know that it's God and not Allah or Buddha? Or Zeus? So kudos to Cameron for his decisions in the film.

The biggest hype about the film was that it was going to reinvent the way movies are made. I disagree. While the 3D enhances the experience of seeing this incredible world, it isn't essential. It's still like any other film that uses shot choices and editing so it isn't really anything new. It's certainly a step forward for the industry, but it isn't the leap they were hoping for.

title: An astonishing movie, strong story, and the most awesome visuals ever!
review:
What an incredible film! Cinematography of the a new era.

Where do I start ? It seems that it's a just perfect sci-fi blockbuster that is at the same time a fairytale, a love story and a battle for survival. But it continues being a (delayed) cry for the slaughtered tribes that used to live in what is now called America or Australia, along with the deforestation and the irrational destruction of our natural environment. And last but not least, it is the 'connection' this all has with us.

Watching Avatar springs into mind a perfect blending of elements and clichés of so many well known movies: Dancing with the Wolves, The Matrix, Born on the 4th of July and Pocahonta to name a few. But I found this to be superb!

All in a future high-tech metaphora, of enormous weaponry and spaceships and a primitive jungle world that's both weird but also so familiar.

Coming to the visual aspects of Avatar, I was simply awed. Its not the first Movie I've seen in 3D recently, but its certainly the best. I think that event if you remove 3D, this movie is an eye candy from start to finish. Simply amazing, but do watch it in 3D before it goes!

title: Just like T2 a milestone for visual effects!
review:
The visual effects in this movie are unseen and bombastic. After a wile you loose this feeling of "it is just a movie". You are immersed in the movie and you are exploring a new world. It is more than one time that you loose your breath. Beautiful images are following each other at high speed and you just can't believe what you are seeing.

The story is a bit thin and predictable though there are nice character developments. But that just doesn't matter because Avatar is just more than a movie, more than a true masterpiece, it is a lifetime experience, a movie that writes film history.

You have too see it in 3D, better IMAX, because the 3D images are a vital part of the movie and it is the way James Cameron intended it.

title: Among the worst pieces of garbage ever made.
review:
This film is horrible.

It reflects modern day Hollywood's total lack of inspiration.

Just make it bling bling and that's it. An uninspired storyline. Corny unlikable characters. No depth.

How can you spent that much money on this crap while thousands upon thousands of people are cued up in food lines all across the US ?

The 3D makes you wanna puke after 30 minutes.

Overrated James Cameron has lost his touch completely. He has become a laughing stock just like Roland Emmerich.

Comparisons made to Peter Jackson are an absolute insult.

I remember films like Piranha 3D, or Friday the 13th 3D. They were both better than this.

You have been warned.

title: If your new bride is blue, just borrow some unobtainium
review:
I rated this movie 3 out of 10. But it deserves at least an 8. I just wanted to protest. A nice movie, a good movie indeed. Very rugged. Flowing. I'm not being sardonic, I really liked it. But its simple, even naive. Simple characters, simple story. One less dimension in the movie, an extra dimension in script won't hurt anybody. A great opportunity wasted I guess. Many talented people, worked hard for many years. So I wanted some depth. I expected something more than a 3D action thriller. Dancing with wolves did have something fresh, something nice. Discrict 9 has xenophobia, racism, bureaucracy, cold corporate mind, and action, friendship, delicious aliens, effects and some gore. It was fresh and surprising and new. Avatar is just big, simple, nice.

I love American S.F. writers. Greg Bear, Theodore Sturgeon, and many more wrote books full of hive minds, planet sized intellects, and with some solid (fictional) science background too. Hall Clement's creatures, P.K.Dicks twisted visions, U.K.le Guin's poetic depth, they are truly amazing. SF opens ones mind. Good SF is also good philosophy, good literature, and it is always good for me. They are hundreds of amazingly disturbing, mind boggling, incredible books out there, but no one dares to touch them. I guess they are too complicated. Ot they prefer not to ruin them, yet.

The story is, an evil, extortionist, capitalist, militarist world company decides to rape a magical planet with good scenery, full of half naked, very long legged girls, (all of them happen to love long walks in the woods, and on the woods, paragliding and horseback riding). But handful of humans seeing the error of their ways decides to lead them to an all out war against invasion. Their strategy consist of throwing things and ramming if possible, shrieking when all else fails. Not very Clausewitzian, and it does not work. But this planet has a hive mind, an alien Gaia, (which has perverse vision of evolution, very fond of feathers and lights, has a touch screen planet-wide, with built in internet). I don't know why but I can picture Mrs. Eywa knitting very bright colored sweaters. When Gaia intervenes it does not intervene gracefully or subtly. Great number of assorted colors of claws, jaws and horns settle the score.

Ecological message, "do not bomb the mother nature, she bites"

Political message "our foreign policy won't change soon"

Mineralogical message "unobtainium does grow on trees"

Military message "use ballistic missiles, drop something from orbit, do not catch arrows"

Possible Na'vi extinction cause "headache, tailache and combinations"

Conclusion "If your new bride is blue, just borrow some unobtainium".

title: A ghastly fire (BOMB)
review:
In some ways this movie is trying to be an adult version of Ferngully the last rainforest. The part of the world inhabited by these creatures, the 'moldy h icans' is like a director's wet dream of Eden, only with attractively plant draped mountains that float (instead of bolting into space). Meanwhile the inhabitants are a wide range of large or stretched versions of creatures we are familiar with: Big big bugs or flying reptiles.

It is a concept flick- man through technology transmits mind into fabricated creature that can live among the intelligent kind of its homeworld. The homeworld has something we (evil humans) want. Humans cannot live on planet but we want a precious material which defies gravity, baldly called unobtainium. The aliens are blue, and look (pick one) like elongated supermodels (every one of them) or cat people with no fur or whiskers. Either way you get wide faces and big yellow eyes right off those 70s paintings on black velvet only with pouty lips. One possibly somewhat original idea is that the intelligent social aliens have tails, at the end of which are exposed nerve fibers that can bond with significantly useful critters to ride, such as a reptilian eyed large flyer, or other critters where the nerve endings might come from other parts of their bodies like a tail to head mind-meld.

I do not recall any of these sharp toothed creatures eating or any significant blood flow from anything. Even the roots of the trees are nerve endings according to the Sigourney Weaver character. Meanwhile, there are no latrines, these natives apparently wander around the vertical environment making nerve contact with wondrous beings but don't need to eat, defecate, raise children, set broken bones, sign contracts, clear leafmold, or establish a government. They don't apparently make music unless they are all arrayed in a large pattern helping the roots save someone's life or convert them to alienhood. It's like woodstock without the rain, the mud, or for that matter, the music. The movie soundtrack was by James Horner who seemed to channel tangerine dream at times, and John Williams at other times. So sometimes the music was spacy, and other times it was star wars.

It goes on for 2 and a half hours and is excruciatingly unbelievable on its own terms. More than the ten bucks, it's the 2 and a half hours I'll never get back and the pained look I could feel on my face as the bad guys were made to look really bad, driving bulldozers ten stories high or trying to destroy an especially important part of the fiber tree of life.

If you loved the self-righteous extermination of the environment to make a point such as "On Dangerous Ground" where the good guys blow up an arctic oil refinery in order to promote environmentalism, this film may resonate with you.

Personally, I think putting the ten dollars to a meal with a lot of fiber in it would have had more agreeable results with a better end product.

title: Good visuals, no plot
review: Visually stimulating, sure. But the most unoriginal plot I've seen in years, not at all creative. Not worthy of the James Cameron label. Unfortunately, I don't see why so many people have gone crazy over this film. Obviously, they were stunned to retardation by all the shiny visuals and brightly colored landscapes in the movie to the point of not realizing that they had seen this exact plot a million times over. There is nothing original in this movie, no creativity in the plot, no in-depth thought or great work of art. It is visually stimulating, and much like a blonde chasing a shiny thing around a room, it is dull and dumb to anyone who has more than 2 brain cells.

title: A lame fairy tale for the gullible
review: Avatar is a lame fairy tale, boring and cringe-worthy, that will appeal only to those who are gullible and easily taken in by an attempt to be fantastical. I love movies and sadly, this one not only bored me to tears but sitting through it was sheer torture, nothing less. And this from James Cameron, whose Terminator and Titanic are my two favorite movies of all time and whose many other films i have seen, loved and admired. The great Sigourney Weaver, who is a class act, delivers a serviceable performance at most. Sam Worthington fares better, although one wishes at times that he had a little more of the charisma of a Leo DiCaprio or a Johnny Depp. Then there is the villain Col Quaritch who is so cartoonish he might have come straight from the pages of a comic book. The biggest tragedy of Avatar is that after all the years and money invested, the final product is so insipid, unoriginal and uninspiring. The music score doesn't come anywhere near John Barry's Dances With Wolves or James Horner's Titanic. And what is most scary is when Hollywood starts making crap movies like this, there is no hope left for mankind.

title: undeserving of any accolades
review:
So here goes another "action thriller" movie which is like any other run-of-the-mill variety except for its 3D sauce.

A far-away planet inhabited by humanoids, who speak (accented English!!), act, walk, emote just like humans on earth, and whose land is rich in some mineral deposits - well the concept of "pandora" may be fine, its cinematography, or should I say rendering is awe-inspiring, use of 3D is innate and hence is simply mesmerizing, but without any story and character it is pure techno-porn.

A battle sequence that is spiced up with motion-controlled robots and fancy looking warships controlled by eye-candy projector screens, deserves a better climax than a knife and bow-arrow fight between the main characters, particularly so when the "winner" is a no-brainer!

Even as a 3D spectacle like "never-before-seen", at ~ 3 hours, even my eyes start feeling the weight of those goggles. To conclude, in my opinion, this is a movie about "How to win the love of a humanoid chick in less than 100 days" - (if you notice carefully, Jake's last video log is numbered 98!) No wonder it drags for so long...

title: ouch.
review:
I felt pretty embarrassed while watching this movie, like more than when I went to see Twilight or Harry Potter. The characters have African accents and features, fake native American ''culture'' including feather head-dresses and using every part of the animal, blue smurf skin and ride around on pterodactyls like Everquest. And they do drum dances to worship a tree god. like, an actual tree that is their god. literally. not as a metaphor, and not a talking tree, just a plain old burnable wooden tree that is also their god.

We are clearly meant to take all this seriously, which is the really sad part: the audience was literally laughing out loud. I mean...I've written some stuff I'd be severely embarrassed to have other people read, and then other people read it, so I can relate to the writer here. I feel bad for him. but STILL.

Everyone keeps saying in the other reviews how much money is involved as if that makes the movie good when to my view it makes the whole situation even more embarrassing. There is no way i could have overestimated this movie's moronicness before seeing it, yet we've mobilized massive amounts of our modern cultural capital squarely behind something that reads like everquest fanfic. I'm a little bit frightened by all the positive reviews---I'm afraid people are going to spot me and say ''you're not one of us'' and either give me a lobotomy or try to eat me.

My favorite character was definitely the corporate overlord. He refers to what they seek as ''unobtainium'' which is an old Usenet/scifi word, and I chuckled because his character was so clued-in and terse in his evilness, made it fun. but then later in the movie he shouts in a serious high-action moment ''the unobtainium is underneath that rock right there!'' and then military dudes fire on the rock, or something, as if the corporate guy doesn't realize it's not actually called unobtainium. That's just a snarky stand-in word for when you're explaining a common story to someone else and want to say ''who cares what it really is,'' when of course it _is_ something specific when you're outside a moment of reflexive exposition. It's like the writer heard some clued people talking to each other, didn't really get what they were talking about but decided he wanted to be just like them, then tried to mimic them. like when a five year old tries to swear like a drunken sailor but doesn't know how to use the words right yet so he sounds all FOB-y, the movie was like that.

also like i said, they have blue skin, talk like continental Africans, and ride around on pterodactyls. please don't forget that part. If you think you can handle this, whatever, go for it.

title: Good movie, but James Cameron's worst.
review:
This was a lousy decade for sci-fi films and I think the 00s have claimed James Cameron, the one person I was counting on to bring back the glory days of the 80s and 90s. What happened to all the Aliens, the Terminators, the RoboCops, the Abysses, the Predators, the Total Recalls, the Jurassic Parks, even The Running Mans? Muscular sci-fi action movies that wowed us with fantastic concepts and visuals while commenting on poignant truths with wit and lack of pretense?

For all those triumphs, James Cameron is my personal film-making hero. Which makes the following all the harder to say: AVATAR is Cameron's weakest film to date. Which isn't to say that it's bad... but it's bad for a James Cameron movie.

First, the story is unoriginal. It's "Pocahontas", plain and simple. The Na'vi, despite being blue and 10 feet tall, are your typical chanting, dancing, Mohawk-sporting, bow-shooting, bead-wearing, body-paint-covered, "Earth-is-our-mother" whooping Indians.

Just pop in a DVD of the 1995 Disney cartoon and count the similarities: Intrepid male soldier who sets off to a new world in search of danger & adventure to test himself? Check. Equally adventurous daughter of the natives' Chief that secretly spies the white soldier exploring her land, befriends him and teaches him the ways of the tribe? Check. The stiff Chief-to-be appointed suitor that the native princess shuns in favor of the white guy? Check. The ensuing fight between the two and arranged execution of the white guy? Check. The white visitors' authority who only cares about money and guns, calling the natives "savages" and launching a final confrontation under false pretenses? Check. The native princess leading the white guy to a sacred tree to ask for advice? Check. The way she then defends the white soldier from her own people as they are about to kill him? Check. Christ, I'm surprised Neytiri didn't break out into song about teaching Jake how to paint with "the colors of the wind".

From what I read, Cameron first wrote this story in 1995, the year the Pocahontas movie came out. Coincidence? Either way, I've seen it all before.

Second, why were the characters so under-developed? Jake and Neytiri's romance feels, at points, shoehorned to forward the plot. Their first meeting: "Why didn't you let me die?" "Because you have a strong heart." Come on, Jim, I know you can do better than that. The point at which they confess their love essentially boils down to "I choose you" "I choose you too" with none of the crafted buildup that led to Jack & Rose's first kiss on the Titanic.

Trudy Chacon. What is her motivation? Why is she helping our heroes? Why is she the ONLY pilot who suddenly (and awkwardly) says "f*** it" and turns away from blasting the Na'vi tree? Does she have friends, insecurities, family? She's just a chick there to quip lines and kick ass.

The bad guys are painfully one-dimensional. Quatrich is a maniac without an ounce of humanity. Think Lieutenant Coffey from "The Abyss", except without the gradual slide into madness from the anger and paranoia. Coffey cried tears before setting off the nuke and that's when you realize the guy is gone... you almost feel sorry for the man before he implodes in his crippled craft. By contrast, Quatrich is a G.I. Joe that likes to blow stuff up for the fun of it. Selfridge is equally limp: just a cardboard cutout of some tie-wearing yuppie who only cares about the bottom line. Do these guys have friends? Ideals? Outside lives? Nope, they're just there as straw men in this transparent social commentary.

Which brings me to: "War on Terror", "pre-emptive strike", "shock and awe". These are words thrown out by the baddies at the finale without anyone so much as blushing, just in case there was any doubt what half the movie's commentary is about. I'm about as anti-Bush and anti-IraqWar as you can get, and these bald-faced references made me cringe. Gone is any masterful subtlety that allows the audience to piece together their own conclusions -- let's simply hammer it into their heads instead. Even Dubya himself was less simplistic than the caricatures portrayed in this movie and this kind of straw-man commentary actually works contrary to the aims of the artist because it paints a picture of someone too evil, too simple, and too unidentifiable to be compared to any kind of actual person, thus letting the real villain off the hook.

I know Cameron is a better writer than this, which is what surprised and frustrated me most of all. So what happened in those 12 years? Maybe the epic battle scenes of the new "Star Wars" and "Lord of the Rings" movies gave him the foolish idea that anyone possibly empathizes with hundreds of faceless pawns getting shot and killed in massive battle scenes while our hero soldier and his beloved warrior princess emerge alive and victorious. Maybe he felt that "District 9", "Iron Man" and "Transformers" didn't amply satisfy our lust for cool CGI battle-bots sequences. Maybe his extended absence has let lesser visionaries like Peter Jackson and Michael Bay set the course for epic adventure cinema and he was merely following suit.

The movie is visually stunning and another landmark achievement in effects. But the same can be said for Star Wars Episodes I - III and I don't see anyone hailing those movies as masterpieces. All in all, with AVATAR, Cameron has again become a pioneer of visual effects... but the complete opposite is true in terms of writing. He has fallen to regurgitating the tired sci-fiction/fantasy plots and concepts of this lackluster decade, forgot how to craft an organic plot and love story, and neglected to hide the marionette strings in his bold social commentary puppet show.

You're still my hero, Jim. I look forward to "Battle Angel" with, for the first time, cautioned optimism.

title: Awful
review: The first thought in my head was: Are you kidding me?! The story is old and well known, predictable and childish. The technology surely is something new but I've got some simple questions: 1.Is it so hard when you make a nice technology to finish the deal with a nice plot?!?!?!(after all some really brilliant movies are in war for the audience attention and they are being judged for so many things other than effects...) 2.Are we supposed to like those ugly bluish creatures just because they seem real?! 3. Rally?No kidding? U actually believe that a naive predictable cliché story should be called "the best movie" even though its just ridiculous: blue creatures on another planet telling us the story of Pocahontas....seriously I feel abused....

title: It doesn't deserve its position nor its score, but...
review:
I still give it a 1/10 because it clearly doesn't deserve 8.6/10 at the global rate and it doesn't deserve to be 53rd in the TOP250.

But this movie is not a waste of time or money. OK, the story is very weak (you don't need to see the movie for the story, you've already seen this over and over again), and the dialogs are weak as well... BUT (and this is a big BUT) you DO want to see this movie in the cinema, with 3D goggles, because it's a masterpiece when it comes to special effects, CGI and 3D. I have no words to describe it, it's mind blowing, that's what I can say.

Besides, this is the first time it has been done so well (3D movie, I mean), so you don't want to be the one in the group talking about it that never saw it properly. This is not a movie to download, this is actually not a movie to really talk about, this is an experience you just won't forget. And even if in a few years we'll have a bunch of 3D-movies very well made that will also blow our minds off, this is the first one, it's a turning point in the film industry, and Cameron deserves the credit of having taken his time to accomplish this spectacle.

title: Avatar is not an original story
review:
Yes, I totally agree with jerichocane-1, Avatar is a remake of Dances with Wolves, but with blue and very tall Indians.

Moreover, there is question in the IMDb FEQ section that says, and I quote:

"Is "Avatar" based on a book?

No. Avatar is based on an original screenplay penned by writer/director/producer James Cameron".

That is not exactly true. Many years ago, in a book of the "The Science Fiction Hall of Fame edited by Ben Bova, I read a story about a crippled man on a wheel chair, mentally connected to a super-being (a feline centaur in this case) who was intended to establish a colony in a very aggressive planet, unfit for human settlers. At the end, the man abandons his wasted human form to live a new, challenging life in the planet. Sounds familiar?

Unfortunately, I remember neither the title nor the name of the writer.

I concede that Avatar has a good creative work regarding the environment in Pandora, but the script is a bad mixture of good old stories.

By the way, wasn't there also a pirate called Cameron?

P.S. Well, I finally found the story. It is Poul Anderson's "Call me Joe", written in 1957.

Please check the link http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_Me_Joe

And I accept that some mediocre script writers find "inspiration" in other people writings, but at least they should have the decency of giving the credit.

title: Excellent 3D, mediocre movie, bad story & bad characters
review:
The 3D of the movie is excellent, especially for someone like me that had never before seen a 3D movie. Graphics and animation are quite excellent. The art in scenery design reminds of Fantasia and is quite impressive.

That is all that is good about this movie. Story wise and ignoring all the Pocahontas/Terra similarities, things are sad. It can't be any more of a cliché. No originality and most importantly the characters are as if made in Hollywood hero molds that have been used thousands of times. The expressions, the language, the characters and the story are incredibly cliché and are really not worthy of being in a movie of such visual & technical achievement.

Avatar could be a Disney movie if it had more depth to it but it fails miserably. I would like to say that I was so overwhelmed by the 3D that it overshadowed the storyline but I can't do that, the story was childish at best. Not to mention that the nice 3D after 2 hours of relentless tacky clichés looses its luster

I am aware of the amazing movie technological advances that result from this movie but no matter how much innovation there is the end result is a bad movie with a bad story combined with bad acting and bad directing covered by nice 3D....IF your theater can support it. (btw when I saw the movie the 3D objects that were closer seemed to flicker but I assume that was a local theater issue)

There are in my opinion plenty of wrong scenes e.g. the huge futuristic spaceships need 6-10 minutes to cover a distance of 2-3 kilometers or where super armor gets pierced by arrows. I don't care if the arrows are much bigger than normal or if the strength of the blue people is immense. Also I don't think the tough chick could abandon battle and say "I didn't sign up for this" and have no consequences....

I cannot imagine any reason to see this (3 hour) movie in the non 3D version. I Would give a much lower rating if there was no 3D version.

The 3D of the movie is excellent and could even justify the ticket cost!!!

Did I mention Sigourney Weaver wakes from a cryo-something-sleep-a-ma-jig? Can anyone spot the similarities of the original script with other Cameron movies nugde-nudge say no more!

If anyone dares defend Cameron that this amazing story of his was in development for so many years and maybe others stole the unique original idea and made Pocahontas/Terra bla bla...please come to your senses!!

I will be happy if I never see a James Cameron movie again!

title: Tired, trite plot line meets high-tech film-making
review:
James Fenimore Cooper meets the 21st century. The Noble Savage theme just will not die. Here, it gets recycled into the "covert operative infiltrates enemy camp and finds out they are nobler than us and changes sides, with tragic consequences" plot line. Moreover, the bad guys are cartoonishly bad and the good guys are utterly without fault, cartoonishly noble. A good movie is one that tells us something true and challenges our understanding of ourselves, our world, our values. In this film, none of the characters has any genuine depth or is even remotely believable. While this may be OK in a mindless action movie, for a film that pretends to be "important", such failings are not forgivable.

The one original part of the movie is the avatar concept. The rest is overdone, anti-Western, neo-pagan claptrap, albeit with genuinely impressive special effects. Somebody out there really knows what to do with a computer.

title: Homo Sapiens and Greed
review:
I was very moved by this film. I saw it as an allegory of what the whites did to the natives in North America, South America, Australia, New Zea land and Tasmania (especially there)--almost complete genocide for the sake of monetary profit by corporate magnates. And since corporations are the real power in developed countries: they have carte blanche to kill as needed. They usually are clever in creating a body of lies that help to dehumanize the victims. (Easier to kill 'em).

The way to drive such a principle home, which means into the heart AND the head, is to show both sides. So we see the natives, Navi, in their culture which includes art, mythology, dance, music, and meaningful rituals. You can come to love any culture (even white European) if you are exposed to this side of humans. And in so doing, it would become horrible to wipe them out for the sake of a fat bank account back home. That is what Cameron does. He gets you on the side of the humanity, in this case, the Navi. (We already know about the dark side of homo Sapiens but it is well sketched in here by the mercenary grunts. I think DANCES WITH WOLVES tells much the same story. There the corporate element stays in the background which was OK for that film.

I was like a little boy visiting a heaven-like world with "people" who were conscious of other things besides money and power. In the back of my mind I wondered that any race could be that harmonious. North American "Indians" treated other tribes horribly in most areas like on the the Plains and conducted raids and wars where there was much cruelty. (See the film THE BLACK ROBE, for a New England version of this.) Were the Navi like that? And what if they were? I guess the question is greed. Given the means would some Navi have exterminated other tribes and gotten rich? They didn't seem to need to be rich.

So are all intelligent bipedal creatures alike? I once heard a theory about why there are no space travelers from beyond--if they became as intelligent as we, they'd also encounter the same jealousies and greed that we have, thus preventing them from combining their resources and cooperating--the infighting would bar them from space travel.

A wonderful epic film. The love story was poetic. The creatures were beautiful and scary. So were the plants. The hero started off a klutz but grew on me. And I liked hearing Wes Studi's voice again. He was the "bad" Indian in DANCES as he was in LAST OF THE MAHICANS.

title: Best movie ever made
review:
The film pops with all the other technical aspects thrown into one. Art Direction is killer as the two worlds blend in perfectly for an acceptable time. The Film Editing is the crowning achievement of the film as it also offers the perfect blend of the two worlds, enticing the viewer and shifting us around. Mauro Fiore is the threat for a Cinematography Oscar this year. It was if the viewer sat down in a chair, put on glasses, and was literally placed on Pandora, spaceships, and floating mountains. The viewer can feel so engulfed by the imagery, you feel like you can smell the leaves from the trees. Avatar is utterly hypnotizing. James Horner's score is some of the best work done in his career. It offers a variable of devastation that moves the viewer to near tears. It goes back to his work on Titanic, where the musical instruments lifted the material immensely. The entire sound team is also locked and loaded for Oscar recognition as the feeling of animals, machines, and arrows buzzing by your head leave you imprisoned in Cameron's exquisite film.

James Cameron has come back home ladies and gentlemen Cameron is back, bigger, badder, and mature in his crowning work of his career. Terminator 2: Judgment Day and Titanic do not even compare anymore. This is the film that can blend the fans of those two films together and lock Cameron into your heart. He's a definite spoiler for a directing bid for the Academy Awards. You have admire the raw, natural talent the man has. How could you ever conceive such an experience and put that much effort and work into it and have it pay off? The box office success will surely keep him in the minds of voters for various critics' awards. His screenplay, leaps and bounds better than 1997's Best Picture Winner, is primed, developed and ripe for the taking. Though, you do acquire the tacky and atypical dialogue you expect from a science fiction director of this caliber, you can appreciate the effort and the honesty of it all. James Cameron is everything Michael Bay wishes he was, to put it bluntly.

Avatar will bring also great actors putting their best foot forward such as Giovanni Ribisi, who is as underrated as they come. Michelle Rodriguez who exudes sexy like any woman starring in a sci-fi epic. Joel Moore, showing his range outside of his comedic work in Dodgeball: An Underdog Story. And the classy veteran actors, CCH Pounder and Wes Studi, who just simply don't work enough.

Avatar is one of the best films of the year. The most exciting, thrilling, and superb work you'll feast your eyes on in any theater this century. Cinema, forever, will remember the benchmark that James Cameron placed not only for himself, but for any man, daring to change the game, the way Cameron did. Avatar is a movie experience to be remembered, and please experience in a movie theater first.

title: it's not a movie! it's like a LUCID DREAM!!! and i don't want to wake up :(
review:
oh my god, i have seen a lot of movies, although there are still a few movies i like more than avatar, but i give avatar a perfect 10/10, and i've never given any movie a perfect score. Avatar deserve a special spot on its own, in that it is not just a movie, it's an experience, watch it in 3d and imax if you can, because you almost feel like you are there. YOU HAVE TO GO SEE IT. PERIOD. It made me depressed afterwards that i have to go back to the normal, boring life again. oh, how much i would give to live in pandora! I also like the romance in the movie, that got me kind of emotional.

ps: don't wait for the DVD, don't watch it on the computer or TV, don't see it in 2d, or even 3d, but see it in IMAX 3D, and i promise you will not regret it.

title: it's just a disappointment.
review:
OK, this is my first review but i am going to be completely honest.

First of all, this movie is predictable. A handicapped marine was given a mission to get close to the clans, eventually fall in love with one of them, then became one of them. Its so predictable it took of all the excitement i had throughout the whole movie! I though it would be a great plot since the budget of this movie was so expensive, so i kept my hopes high. In the end, it ends up just as mentioned. Disappointed...

Secondly, the CGIs. This can actually be an animation since almost every scene is completely in CGI. And the CGI even looked cartoon-ish. The characters looked cartoon-ish,the creatures looks cartoon-ish. The only thing I enjoyed in this movie is the scenery. (Hence the 3, it would be a 2 if it wasn't for the scenery.) It's not a bad movie actually,it's watchable. I just think with the given budget it could be just a lot better,a way lot better movie than this.

title: A really really good looking corpse
review: Avatar as a visual exercise is a masterpiece,however that should not distract from the terrible dialogue and boring storyline.It is an overlong and dreary rehash of a story that has been done before. The only character I could relate to was colonel Quaritch,about halfway through this funeral of a film I was hoping he'd succeed in slaughtering the blue shits and end the film. Unfortunately Its a Disney money making piece of sh-it, with hundreds of millions spent on marketing to convince the unwashed masses to put down their cheese burgers and turn off the X-factor/American idol.So the "good guys" have to win and colonel Quaritch dies(*sob*) before he can kill the human traitors and save the world. Only see this if you HAVE never seen 3D,other then that its a waste of time.

title: This is whats wrong with America!
review:
I have tried to watch this movie countless times. I HATE it more and more each time I TRY to watch it. I ask all my friends what is so good about it. They all tell me the same thing "It is the most beautiful movie ever". Well that is a load of crap. I am an old school fan (as you can tell by my name) I like movies with great Stories and amazing acting, which this movie had neither.And as far as making the military look bad!!!! Are you serious!!!! I am 100 percent baffled at how this movie made any money. Oh because it "looks pretty" we should go see it. You know what looks pretty Jennifer Lopez but everyone hates Gigli!

Do not take this review as i hate James Cameron because I don't mind the guy at all.
