So, I've seen it. I am a big SF fan, I saw almost all SF movies and series made in the past 30-40 years or so.

However, Avatar did not impress me that much. The story is just a classic "humans are bad" tale, with a scientist who is not listened to ... too typical and too old story. So if you are looking for a great story, look somewhere else.

On the other hand, the special effect, the view, the blending of reality with CGI is perfect. You almost can't tell what is real and what is not. For the hole view and CGI I give this movie a 10, but for story I give it a 0, so the result is a 5 from me.

For one, I consider this a great entertainment, this is a must see movie, but I will not watch it again, that's for sure.

title: Visually Stunning, But Not A Film I'd Remember
review:
This film contains the greatest special effects I've ever seen. I'm glad I didn't see it in 3D, or I'd be having headaches.

"Avatar" takes place in the year 2154. Earth has run out of resources and they have come to a distant moon, Pandora, to get Unobtainium to save their dying planet. However, the natives on Pandora, the Na'vi, are unwilling to give up their land. Handicapped marine Jake Sully is part of the Avatar Project, a project in which humans transfer their consciousness to their Na'vi counterpart to aid in relocating the Na'vi residing on the biggest deposit of Unobtainium in the area.

Although the storyline sounds promising, and it is a rare film in which the earthlings are cast as the villains, this film is forgettable. You'll never forget the effects, but as a film itself, it just disappears as you watch it.

title: Eh, kind of disappointed
review: Okay, so before all of you out there who love this movie as much as I love some other movies say anything, let me just say what I have to say. I didn't love the movie, I didn't hate the movie. I was transformed into the world of Pandora and boom, the movie was over before I knew it. I felt it was very entertaining, however, have we not seen this movie a million times before? Sure the special effects were phenomenal, but I am at a point where I wish directors and companies would stop relying so much on special effects and more on a story. I get what it is trying to tell us. The religious aspect, the ecological aspect, race, love, freedom....the list goes on. I get it. I won't even criticize the acting. I am just at a point where I feel that special effects are beginning to control the movies that are made for us, not the director/producer/studio. When do you ever hear during a trailer, "the greatest story you'll ever see?" Never, you always hear" With groundbreaking effects." The greatest film of all time? I think not.

title: It's a great movie....But not really the kind that amazes me
review:
When I first watched Avatar in the cinemas, I actually thought it was a really good sci-fi flick. Because it's got a good mix of visual and special effects, a good story, convincing character development etc. But what I find most interesting in this movie is the social commentary of corporate greed and respect for other people's cultures and beliefs, I can see that James Cameron is using the saying "Money is the root of all evil" as the device that keeps the story going.

Yet despite of all the Awards that the movie received I personally think that it is just one of your typical sci-fi movie. Overall I think that this movie is very good but overrated.

title: Disappointing
review: Avatar had the potential of being transcendent, but falls well short of it. It had the opportunity of really getting inside the mind that is not just in harmony with nature, but co-creative with it. --Of getting an up-close-and-personal sense of a Gaia in all its magnificence. --Of contrasting all that with our relatively impoverished, modern consciousness. What we got instead was the tired old good guys against bad guys drama, dressed up with a lot of effects, special as they were. Even the indigenous culture, supposedly the nature people, partook of the same fight-against-the-other-guy mentality that our culture is trying to outgrow. There were no redeeming solutions offered. Most characters, colorful as they may have been, were just black and white caricatures. I really wish I could praise this one, but I just can't. Such a magnificent effort, and such a pity.

title: Spectacular battle scenes and exotic creatures; plot wasn't bad
review:
I play World of Warcraft and saw similarities with parts of the game such as the Navi race being much like elves, and there being exotic creatures like dragons, and the exotic environment. I liked it a lot because of that. I am big on action movies, too.

I saw this first in '2D', and then '3D'. I didn't like as much in '3D'. '3D' is a misnomer. They can bring forward certain items by tricking the eye, but what I do naturally is to look at items other than the forward items, and they are many times simply are out of focus, so my mind doesn't buy it. That's just me though. They really need to focus on the item being brought forward. There were lots of forward items out of focus. There were large segments of the movie with no items moved forward. Maybe that's by design because it might get pretty irritating to some people.

The best part of the movie is when the hero swoops down on the most powerful creature on the planet and lands it in front of the tribe. The sense of leadership, empowerment and inevitability were awesome. The sheer size of the mining equipment, the robot warriors and large military hovercraft, not to mention the sound with it all was awesome.

I have to say I disliked some terminology used in the movie. I am a liberal (but not big on environmentalism) and this is an extremely liberal movie but phrases were used like 'fight terror with terror'. We know the colonel is a evil jerk and don't need a ridiculous phrase like that to prove it to us. The precious metal being sought is called 'unubtanium'. Ha! Don't get me wrong, I agree that republicans and too many military leaders are too arrogant and stupid to realize colonialism and imperialism by invasion simply does not work, some of the references were ridiculous and caused a pure story to be partly impure and laughable. I was having a nice dream with this movie and then these phrases had to 'wake me up' to reality.

Another ideal presented by the movie is that all nature is one, and that it 'thinks' as one. Note I support much conservation that occurs, more than most people in the USA. However, a government or political party, person (such as those participating in this movie or funding it) claiming they care about nature so much, I don't buy it. There is much self-serving going on with that. We all know people buy a feel good message even if it's completely fictional. Humanity is currently a significant and totally 'natural' aspect of the environment, including all our pollution, machines and military. Environmentalism is simply getting way too overrated. It's on the bubble. Start caring about human beings more than cute little creatures. Certain not-so-pleasant to look at species 'invade' an area and crush the weak and become dominant. They are invasive species. It happens. Accept it.

title: Good, not great
review:
Overall, it's a good movie, but not a great film. I see this, more or less, as the Star Wars of our generation. It's a visual effects spectacle that's all the more astounding given that the setting is an alien planet. As Sam Worthington's character familiarizes himself with the planet, we sit in awe of the beautifully detailed scenery and the impressively animated creatures. Certain scenes become all the more better thanks to the visual effects.

However, the story fails to match up to the lush visuals. The film essentially boils down to environmentally-friendly natives fighting against the evil invaders and their bad machines. Most of the characters are not compelling enough for you to care about them, especially the protagonist - Sam Worthington's character is nothing more than another dumb soldier-turned-rebel hero. Sigourney Weaver's character, with her caustic wit, and Michelle Rodriguez's character, with her steely nerves, are by far the best of the bunch; the other characters are mostly ho-hum.

I think James Cameron was trying to make this movie as palatable as possible to all cultures, which would explain the clichéd storyline and the dry characters. Movies like these focus more on visuals and battle scenes. Crafting a good script or building a truly memorable cast of characters comes second, unfortunately.

Good movie, but not a great film.

title: Fights with my favorite movie of all time.
review:
My favorite movie of all time has always been Star Wars from 1978. This movie is the first movie to ever make me even think about it. I've seen dozens of movies I've liked, and this is the first that has gone beyond liking it to loving it. I first went to see this a little over a month ago, not having very high expectations. But man, was I wrong.

The story begins by pretty much introducing the main character, Jake Sully. His brother who was supposed to go to Pandora, a moon in the closest Star System from Earth, was killed. Since Jake has identical DNA, he is offered to take his place. Since the Earth is suffering in a bad economy, and Jake has a broken back, he takes the offer. The moon is inhabited by dangerous animals, and a local native humanoid group called the Na'vii.At first, Jake does not care for them at all. But at the end, he is willing to give his life for them.

I believe this movie shows a transformation of a character from an arrogant attitude, into a feeling that he's willing to give his life for. When Jake reaches Pandora, he has an arrogant and bad attitude. He doesn't care about the Natives. He doesn't care about the operation. He just wants to get his legs back. At the end of the film, Jake has completely broken away from assisting his sergeant, who wants to get rid of the Natives. Accompanied by two scientists and a marine, Jake sets out to save the local Natives from their undying doom.

It's still playing at three different show times here in Pennsylvania. If it's still showing in your town, go see it. I'll be seeing it for the third time this weekend.

title: Pretty pictures a good movie do not make
review:
Avatar is quite the paradox.

On one hand you have a film of such stunning, breathtaking technical skill and imagination, that it should, and almost certainly will, reap several top awards at the Oscars, to go with its $2.5 billion (and counting) worldwide gross.

On the other, you have a unoriginal, almost dull story which has somehow been stretched to a excruciating 3 hours! James Cameron is a visionary. This is not a revelation. 3D is a gimmick. This not a revelation either. But surely he needn't have relied on a fad that has come and gone many times over the years, and will continue to do so til the same effect is achieved without the glasses. Fads have their time in the sun though, and Avatar's position at the top of box office charts attest to this. Here though, it's an unnecessary distraction. Maybe that's it point.

Furthermore, how will Avatar be seen in five or ten years time? When the marvels of its technical achievements become commonplace, Avatar will surely be seen as an overblown, dumb action flick that simply doesn't have enough assets to warrant another viewing. Remember the first time you saw the dinosaurs in Jurrasic Park? Like the characters, i was stunned. It's a goddamn dinosaur! That memory stays with me, and I still enjoy the movie, because it's a thrill ride and a great adventure story, even though CGI is now as common as Windows.

Sadly, Avatar will be recalled for its breakthrough technology, but when that novelty becomes the norm, i doubt much else will raise an eyebrow.

title: Good But Not Great
review:
I was anticipating this movie for a long time. I saw it in theatres, not 3D just regular.

I wasn't "blown away" like most people were. I was expecting more from Cameron, but I guess he couldn't get as much out of his CGI animated actors.

The movie was visually stunning, and I loved the premise. It seemed like allegory for what is going on today in the middle east in terms of displacing populations for resources. I really liked that. I liked the fact that U.S marines were toppled by the natives. I liked the message of the movie. How we are all linked to our planet and each other.

The movie is about humans travelling to another star system in search of a precious mineral that is worth it's weight in gold x 1000. How ever there is a problem, the biggest reserves are under the home of the native population...in typical U.S fashion they dispatch the marines to destroy the natives.

The avatar is a genetically modified body that looks like the aliens but is controlled remotely by humans. The human controlling the main character loses himself in the alien culture and soon is forced to choose sides. Beautiful story..just like Pocahontas, or the Last Samurai.

This movies gets high marks for visuals and allegory...however the story was typical, and CGI doesn't convey emotions like real humans...therefore I'm giving it a 7 out of 10, I wouldn't want to see this again, but it was worth seeing the first time.

title: Pocahontas on a different planet
review:
I really don't understand everybody being so hysterical about this movie. the story contains nothing more than Pocahontas or any Disney movie. man goes to tribe for the benefit of his own people, falls in love and walks over to the other side.

the images are quite nice but very overrated, i saw this movie in 3d but normal would've been pretty much the same. although it has become a nice film but not really more than that.

Maybe i'm sounding a little too negative but thats a reflection to the massive hype going around on this movie. of course it has it's good moments and cool things.

the most ridiculous thing is without a doubt the stupids that became depressive after seeing this movie cause this planet would be so beautiful. really how dumb/stupid/emo have you got to be to say something like this. i suggest the 'earth' documentary's!

title: Technically brilliant
review: I've waited a long time for an opportunity to see "Avatar" and I've been eagerly anticipating it. Technically, in terms of the absolutely amazing visual effects and the use of 3D, it was fantastic, I've never seen anything like it. I was mesmerised by the illuminated vegetation and of course the amazing animals. The 3D was superb and really enhanced the film, instead of just being a gimmick. From the point of view of the story, as a science fiction fan of some 50 years, I have to say it didn't strike me as terribly original, in fact parts of it were a pastiche of concepts distilled from decades of SF novels. Some little touches like the six-legged horses came straight from Robert Heinlein's "Glory Road", for example, and I could name a couple of dozen dragon-riding tales. That apart, it was still a thought-provoking film and overall I found it a most enjoyable experience. I wasn't disappointed.

title: The return of a Man called Horse
review: Let me say first of all that this movie is really well done and well worthy for its message is quite educative. I read that it was visually stunning and my friend told me the same. A joy for your eyes? yes, absolutely! but is that enough? In my opinion this movie lacks in originality: most ideas seem to be taken from "A Man Called Horse" a film by Elliot Silverstein, with Richard Harris, done in 1970. Other ideas remind me of "The Emerald forest" by John Boorman, "Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within" (Eywa is the same of Gaia!) and "Pocahontas" (who inspired the character of Neytiri). All these movies had more pathos and had been far away more original than Avatar, even because in their own ways said something new. Don't get me wrong, there is nothing wrong in getting ideas somewhere else, or in doing remakes, but don't expect too much enthusiasm from moviegoers with good memory (like me). I would like to add one last thing. For some reasons I still like to find some acting in the movies I watch, and when the main characters are computer done, or wear heavy make-up or masks, I find it difficult to feel any emotion, even when special effects are extraordinary, like in this case.

title: The tagline says it all: Enter the World
review:
In 1999, the Wachowski brothers made a science fiction action movie which changed the face of action for a good five years as suddenly now every movie had to have this new thing called bullet-time, which is ironic since bullet-time is essentially proto-cinematic and the first "movement tests" of Muybridge circa 1880 were the exact same thing as bullet-time. The theme of The Matrix was essentially technophobic despite its game-changing technological spectacle because it said outright, "Don't take that blue pill, get out of dream land and live in the real world. The sucky, barren, survivalist real world that is so much more worth saving than your tasty steak-filled dreamland." Exactly ten years later Cameron comes out with a movie about saving the environment and the killing off of our connection with the earth, but the entire narrative is developed through the titular thematic component, avatars. And no, not just the Na'Vi avatars. EVERYBODY in this movie has an avatar. The big bad meany boss commando is never more comfortable unless he's in his Cameron-favorite Mechwarrior. The Na'Vi download themselves right into the creatures of the forest. The ore-miner general uses his corporation as his avatar. The problem is that through all of this downloading, virtual recreation, and multiple personalities is that the theme of re-connecting to the world gets lost in the pure desire to log into a different outward appearance of one's self, which is never deconstructed, but in fact reinforced by the Na'Vi's own spiritual uploading of personalities between bodies. The weird thing is that the whole idea that the world of Pandora is a giant synaptic brain really never seems to be of consequence until the battle at the end, except that we're just supposed to believe in it based on what characters say, not what is shown. Whereas The Matrix makes it's downloading program quite clear from the, uh, intro screen. You know, that famous intro screen? Pandora never really makes its presence known except for an action sequence. I'm just sayin'.

The only two quotes that mattered: "I see you now." And, "Now real life felt more like the dream." These are the rough equivalents to The Matrix's "Why do my eyes hurt?" and "Stop trying to hit me and hit me." Therefore, as much as I'm not really as critical of other people about Avatar's storytelling and themes (it's all archetypical and not worth getting upset over or endless comparisons to similar story lines), I just feel it's necessary to point out that wherein the medium is the message, the message of Avatar is "Log in." It's a technophiliac celebration of virtual reality, and functionally so. I do not, in fact, consider that to be a negative thing or really criticize that approach, I just feel with the amount of attention this movie is getting, I have not really heard that acknowledged. So going to those people who are sad 'cause Pandora ain't real--it is, in fact, functionally dialectic to the experience of the film. Wherein fan culture develops through cultural events such as this film, I see Avatar as predominantly an invitation, and it's one that the world has seemed to accept. So now that the game has changed and 3D is the blockbuster motif, it is time to start reappraising fantasy worlds and figure out how to immerse the audience into truly alternative realities than simply escapist worlds.

--PolarisDiB

title: Sensational film viewing!
review:
Sensational it is! I definitely give this film top marks!

It is quite rare for a movie of such a large scale to leave such a large impression on me. If you are a fan of big blockbuster hits, sci-fi meets action, or even James Cameron himself, then I definitely recommend Avatar.

Avatar ticks all the required boxes. Unique. Fun. Dramatic. Action packed. It definitely has something for a varied audience. Though, the ultimate stand-out of the film, is the vast and expansive world that it is set in. The detail that has been put into "Pandora" is exceptional and mind blowing, and all the praise goes to James Cameron and his team. Once you see the film you will know what I mean, it feels as if you are captured in the moment, it feels as if you are involved in the adventure that is: Avatar.

title: Probably the BEST movie of the decade
review: It was actually not a surprise to see James Cameron's new offering "Avatar" breaking the Box Office records.This movie is probably the best movie of the decade. After 12 years director James Cameron has returned to the film making and by every means it's not difficult to say that he's back with a bang.Avatar just doesn't limit itself to the C.G. effects but it's the entire plot that makes this movie a pure masterpiece.Unlike Michael Bay's movies which are more oriented in special effects than the story itself.But Cameron's "Avatar" is a brilliant mixture of special effects with a great storyline.Entire thing about the movie is amazing..the storyline,the background score and esp. the direction. I doubt this movie to be what it is had it been directed by Michael Bay.But Cameron has shown his brilliant display to capture a great plot with suitable special effects and clever direction.I myself felt amazingly pleased to having watch this movie. So without saying any further i just want to recommend this movie to everyone...if u still haven't watched this movie then you'll terribly regret it. i give it straight 10 out of 10

title: Avatar: A cinematic milestone (In production, not story)
review:
I was expecting great things when I saw this movie. Cameron was working on this movie for 10+ years before its release in theatres. Great things I saw. A good movie shines in many of its categories including acting, cinematography, writing, and story.

The cinematograophy, art direction, and effects were what made this movie for me. I respect cameron's patience in working on this film.

The acting wasn't bad, but it wasn't amazing. Sam Worthington (like any rising star) still has a way to go. I expect bigger and better things from him in the future. Sigourney weaver did her part as did ribisi and the military general (cant remember his name).

The writing and story was what everyone overlooks. It was cliché. A good message, yet i felt like it was an anachronistic performance of pocahontas or ferngully. Greed was a huge theme in the film and it was shoved down the throats of many corporations and others who sacrifice beauty for money. Its all about the benjamins (which is why this film will win best picture) and this film did a good job showing it, yet only took it a step further through the way it was presented: the animation, not through the srcipt or general story.

In no way do i think it deserves an Oscar because it lacks in a fair amount of categories. Regardless, its a cinematic experience in terms of its visuals. 6.5 of 10 (I round up).

title: Exceeded my expectations....
review:
... Which I must admit were not too high. I'm generally not a fan of sci-fi, and especially can't stand computer generated graphics in a movie. And predictably, I hated it at the start of the film. It all looked like a glorified cartoon. But soon enough I got immersed in the story and forgot about the cartoonish presentation.

I am generally a total sucker for movies about indigenous, 'primitive' people. In fact I'd love to learn from them how to live in the wild in various parts of the world, with no job, no mortgage, just hunting, gathering, and finding my place in nature and using its resources with skill. My favourite all-time movie is Apocalypto.

So it's no surprise really that this film entertained me. I'm not too fussed about 3D and the technical aspects, like I said if you don't get into the story, then it all looks like a video game, rather than a film.

Heard comments that this is as Anti-American movie. Hmmm I don't know, the movie certainly made heaps of money to some globalist Americans in Hollywood. Go figure. Maybe the makers are so arrogant they don't care what people think, as long as they get their money. I think the global market is increasingly anti-imperialist and eco-conscious, and the producers saw a demand for such a movie. Lucky for us. But wait till you can watch it cheap.

title: Review of Avatar
review: While watching James Cameron's Avatar I didn't feel like I was simply viewing another film but I felt as if I was in the middle of a one-of-a-kind experience. In a similar fashion to how The Matrix (1998) raised the bar for technology in cinema in the late 90s, Avatar has now raised the level even higher. Throughout the entire film I was amazed at how gorgeous the planet of Pandora looked as well as the blue natives and the human made machines brought to occupy the newly found planet. Not since Star Wars (1977) has a more fascinating world been created. As far as the plot goes, it basically has the same story as Dances with Wolves (1990) and The Last Samurai (2003), which is not necessarily a bad thing. However, lets face the facts, the reason to go see Avatar is not for the plot but it is to see the amazing digital technology. Though it is almost three hours, Avatar is like a roller coaster that keeps you on the edge of your seat for a long period of time except there is no long line, no quizzy stomach, and no screaming people behind you (except for the occasional screaming baby that some dumb parent thought was good idea to bring to the movie theater). Throughout the last decade I have had my hesitations about filmmakers overusing special effects (such as in the new Indiana Jones and 300). However, after seeing Avatar I am excited about the use of modern technology in film. Avatar has demonstrated that through the use of CGI new worlds can be created and look almost realistic. In short, you need to go see Avatar on the big screen, with the 3D glasses, and with a large popcorn and a drink. Avatar is why people go to the movies, to be entertained beyond words.

title: Generally good but it does have flaws
review:
I have finally seen "Avatar" after two months into its release. Even so, the whole cinema was packed. Its success as the highest grossing film (not taking inflation into account) is highly understandable. It is in many ways the perfect popcorn movie - action, adventure, romance and a stirring score. The heroes are easy to like and the villains are easy to hate. The world created is enchanting and breathtakingly beautiful; every flower and plant and tree brims with beauty, and the use of motion capture is perhaps the best done so far.

As successful as the film may be, and no matter how many Oscar nominations and Golden Globe wins it may have, "Avatar" is however not without flaw. Its script often seems a bit secondary to the action and flashy graphics, and the film overall does go on for perhaps a bit too long, a problem that has plagued many a James Cameron film. Although the climax is truly exciting, the final act starts off quite poorly and it does become quite boring at this point. Equally, the level of myth creating does result in some somewhat unbelievable and ridiculous moments; the scene of Navi-mating did, quite frankly, leave me laughing a tiny bit.

Yet as imperfect as it may be, "Avatar" is overall a good film and worth watching - make sure you go and see it in 3D on the big screen before its run ends as well, as it truly gives the film a most fascinating scope.

title: Absolutely Amazing and Immersive
review:
If there was but one word I could use to describe "Avatar", it would be: IMMERSIVE. Right from the beginning, the viewer is drawn in to the experience. There have been greater epics, larger explosions, and more amazing stories created in American cinema. Yet, James Cameron has succeeded in creating something far more spectacular: a truly immersive world.

J.R.R. Tolkien could be considered a forerunner to world building. The realm of Middle Earth is as fantastic as it is vast, full of wondrous works of dead civilizations, heroes, villains, and common folk. Peter Jackson did a fantastic job of bringing those thoughts and words to life. The epic adventure of "Lord of the Rings" was great, but it was always lacking in the world it created. It never felt far, far away or different, especially if one already knew most exterior shots were performed in New Zealand. Cameron took this idea of a fantastic, alien world and literally brought it to the stars.

The world of Pandora was simply stunning and beautiful. The amount of work that was put in to creating something like it is unbelievable. What I found most awe inspiring was how the world consumed me. Thanks to the 3D picture, things swirled and danced around the frame's object of focus. I truly felt "there". Above all else, I believe that is what Cameron was aiming for. "Avatar" can be topped in many ways in the future; indeed it is painfully obvious (literally if you wear glasses, like me) that this 3D film-making is still in its infant stages. The only place for it to go is to advance further. Yet, I think Hollywood, and even Cameron himself, will be hard pressed to top the world of Pandora in the foreseeable future.

Now, onto the bad, what little there is.

The Na'vi are essentially Native American Indians. Their speech, clothing (what little exists ;-) ), mannerisms, and fundamental beliefs are basically a carbon copy of Native American culture. However, this doesn't hurt the experience much as it works well. I don't know of any other culture that could have made a better match for the Na'vi.

Some of the acting feels plastic and scripted, like something out of a 70's or 80's movie. When tragedy struck the Na'vi, it didn't feel very real; I guess that's the problem with CGI and voice acting: it can't always properly portray emotion.

In closing, "Avatar" is truly a great work of art, and a must see for any fan of sci-fi or epics.

title: Great Film!
review: I went and saw this film in IMAX and 3D, and man I was blown away! The visuals were absolutely stunning. The landscapes looked so real, I couldn't believe they were CGI. James Cameron is a great director. It's also nice to see a blockbuster that isn't based on a book, existing story, or a continuation of a franchise. I've read on this site that people are complaining about the storyline that it's a ripoff of another movie. Give me a break! Don't you guys know there hasn't been a truly original story since The Odyssey and The Iliad. All stories after have borrowed from those two stories. Well you can't please everyone. Every movie has borrowed from something.

title: Plot is same as an old Indian movie
review:
The plot is same as an old Indian movie - Vietnam colony

title: Amazing creativity
review:
I am not a tremendous fan of the whole 3-D thing because most of it doesn't appear 3-D to me and it makes watching the movie really difficult. I wasn't really excited that my son wanted to see it in 3-D and I was even more skeptical when I discovered that there was an additional $3.50 charge for this version of the movie. However, after the movie started and I put on the required glasses, I was blown away. Avatar 3-d does not fit even loosely into the boring, hard-to-watch realm as other purported 3-D films.

This is by far the absolute best movie I have ever seen. The creators have really outdone themselves with this movie. The level of action is right where it should be, the drama is perfect, the story line is understandable, and the special effects are right on target. I didn't find a single thing I could say negatively in regards to this movie. Even the extra $3.50 per ticket we had to pay was worth getting to experience this.

Love the movie and would see it again and be just as thrilled as the first time. The Real 3-D is just so unbelievable that you actually feel like you are in the movie. I found myself a couple of times dodging things that were flying off the screen at me. Several times I noticed that the theater as a whole was saying "Wow!" or "Holy *#(@*^" out loud.

Amazing, amazing, amazing.

title: More than a message... A warning to the world
review:
James Cameron leaves not only one, but lots of messages with this outstanding work, in a beautiful way.

The first thing that most people remember when trying to make analogies with our real world is the colonization of America, when white man came and eradicated the natives with absolutely no mercy. That's OK, but there's much more than this.

In fact, there are stories like that happening till this very day. In tribal regions of Asia, "missionaires" and "development associations" claim to bring "the word of God" and "progress" to the natives, while taking their lands, enslaving the children and destroying their culture.

Besides, it makes us think about our own society and the way we live. Our way of life is based in an endless need for resources, like they were infinite. We seek to explore everything from the land, not only mineral and biological resources, but even humans as well.

That's why Sully - and the crowd - fall in love with the world of Pandora and the Na'vi people. They live in perfect equilibrium with nature, as part of it, not "owners". They live as equals - brothers and sisters, in absolute respect for each other. No one has more rights than another. To live in such kind of society in a world of total freedom would be really like a dream - a dream we must all fight for, just as Sully. It's not like "progress" is our enemy. The point is, we must stop and think what "progress" really is. That's the kind of questions that Cameron brings to us.

If we persist in living this way, we'll be soon in a "dying world", just like said Jake.

title: The movie now is beyond reviews
review: The movie now is beyond reviews, It has broken all box office records. It shows the iniciative be getting people engaged with cinema again using 3d technology. The effects of the movie were really great enjoyed the whole film. I wouldn't say its the best movie I ever say, special effects don't engage all the passions on the viewer, you also need good acting and plot. But it is a work of art, very detailed during the whole movie, and by no means boring. Not a movie you would buy a pirate copy or download a torrent, you have to see it on the big screen in 3D or you really will not have seen the movie. It seems to have sparked a love-hate mindset, maybe those who hate it had too high expectations, I went to see it after hearing about it for 2 months and had to see what all the fuss was about, well it was well worth the money. This will be the start of many 3D productions bring people back to the cinema.

title: Films Like This Are The Reason I Go To The Movies!
review:
Avatar is a fantastic accomplishment in film making. Most of the reviews comment on the visual power of the film. (It must be experienced in 3D and I have no doubt that we will see more and more films made in 3D.) Avatar is absolutely visually stunning, but that is not what makes this a great film in my opinion.

The story makes the film! It seems that it has become the popular thing to do to say that the story is weak and it has been told many times before. Sure, love stories have been told countless times in film. Struggles between good and evil have been told thousands of times in film. I think it is ridiculous to fault Avatar as a mediocre story. It is a powerful and moving story. It is a story that keeps you on the edge of your seat completely engaged in the film. My wife and I didn't want the story to end. In fact we saw it a second time and as a testament to the quality of the story, we both liked it even more the second time around.

It has become popular to say Avatar is shallow tree hugging propaganda. In my opinion that is just people trying to find fault with a film that has become incredibly successful. I don't want to give anything away, but I will say that even though the themes of the film are nothing new, the story is told with perfection. The visual experience in amazing, and it is amazing because all the film making technology is used to tell a wonderful story.

title: Honest review
review:
This 'story' is laughably transparent. I think within 10-15 minutes of watching the movie, I could have mapped out the rest of the plot and that was after missing the first 20 minutes. My dad is a frequent movie-goer and his review of the movie was "It was essentially a live action Ferngully." The movie takes a very safe a predictable path from start to finish without the slightest hint of a plot twist. There really is no point to click "Contains Spoiler" when writing a review for this movie because there aren't any.

The obvious point that pulls this rating up from a 1-2 in my mind was seeing it in 3D Imax. You really feel like you are part of this world if you have a decent seat in the theater and don't suffer from motion sickness. If you let visual spectacle draw you in, the three hours will fly by and you'll remember at the end that you should probably go use the bathroom before your kidneys explode.

What frustrates me is that this movie will probably clean up at the Oscars despite having an unoriginal story. Best Picture, not even close, Best Visual Effects, no brainer.

title: Excellent movie :)
review:
*maybe little spoiler*

I heard that "Avatar" was brilliant from my friends and so many reviewers. I was actually quite nervous of seeing it. Because I had such high expectations.

"Is it as good as everybody says?" I went to the cinema's with a friend who has already seen it. She said it was great. Since she's seeing it again with me.

The whole day for the cinema's was full. We both saw it on 3-D. we were lucky to get in. 2 and a half hours exiting the cinema when it ended. I LOVED IT! I was not disappointed.

The beautiful, charming world of Pandora. Was so realistic and beautiful. Especially at night where everything glows. The 3-D enhanced the surrounding area made it almost look realistic.

The motion capture of the characters was also incredible. Their movements flow with the movement of creatures in real life. Their expressions were also carefully looked at. Zoe Saldana did an excellent job as Neytiri. You can really see her pain through betrayal and sadness of losing an important part of her world.

Sam Worthington also did a good job as Jake Sulley. he has few small funny parts of the movie. But he did a great job as the main character.

But the story completely lacks originality. The story seems to have taken bits of Pocahontas, Ferngully and Dinotopia. The only thing different is that it's Sci-Fi oriented and they go a bit further into defeating their enemies and showing more tragedy. Some bits and reasonings might also seem far fetched. But hey it's a movie! ENJOY IT! XD the war scene was mega awesome!

I was not really impressed with some of dialogue though. "Juujuu berries" or "Daisy Cutters". You can easily think of things for them to say other than that. Especially with the things that they were talking about.

The score of the movie done by James Horner. Might not be the best score ever heard. But it suites the movie perfectly. I liked it and that I got the soundtrack.

I loved the movie. My grandfather took me to see it again this time in IMAX 3-D. Since he wanted to see it. He also enjoyed it.

It is a great spectacle of a movie. And I clearly advise to go see it. But if you don't want to see anymore save the environment movies......then don't see it.

I'm going to buy it once it comes out on DVD

title: Absolutely Fantastic
review:
That movie was without a doubt the best movie i've seen in the 21st century. James Cameron made a brilliant effort. The storyline was good, the characters they chose were good and the colour and creatures were just brilliant. And for once other species didn't come to us, we went to them.

Sam Worthington did a brilliant job. he really showed us how great he is and he portrayed his character perfectly.

James Cameron used 10 years to make this and it was 10 years of his life well spent. To use 237 Million dollars just for 1 movie is just great and the profit is probably over 2 billion by now. But you know when you see Titanic, you say i've got to go see Avatar for one reason, because of James Cameron.

I rated this a 10 out of 10 because of everything i listed above and because it had a moral, if there are species out there, we should leave them alone because they are not doing anything to us.

Well done Cameron.

title: Greatest Presentation of Perennial Philosophy of All Time
review: I am just back from my second viewing of Avatar in 3D and in my opinion it is the greatest movie of all time. The fact that it is the most visually stimulating movie I have ever seen is only one part of its impact. It is a call to all aware humans to rally in defense of the webs of life on our planet. This is the most important issue and message of our era and this movie expresses it with a subtle beauty that has taken me to a new level of understanding. The movie points to the fact that it will take a new awareness, a balanced, big picture awareness that includes all human capacities, not just intellectual, to address our global problems.

title: Based on classic novel
review:
The biggest complaint that I have read about this movie is that it has a shallow, mediocre plot.

About half way through the film I realized I have read this story before. I reminded me of a Harry Harrison novel Deathworld which I read when I was in college. Harrison wrote a series of novels and a short story based on the characters in Deathworld, which was the first novel in the series. I always thought that the Deathworld series was some of the best SF I have ever read.

I subsequently learned that indeed Camaron based his movie on Deathworld. (Note: I have not been able to go through all the reviews to see if anybody else picked up on this.) If one thinks the plot is silly, do not read Deathworld. You would probably would not like it either.

title: Brilliant, fabulous, brave.....energetic
review: While watching this movie, Avatar, the first thing that came to my mind was Incredible and I don't know how to describe this movie but I'll try. As a lover of Sci-fi genre I watch all these kind of movies like Spiderman 3, Ironman, Pandorum and all of them were really nice and I enjoyed but they all were something I would say expected, known and simply nice movies but this movie made me sure that Hollywood will always be on the top because of these amazing producers, directors who don't only have brilliant ideas but also the guts to make them come to life and show to us. First of all this movie had everything innovative and second great thing about it was that these innovations were not like showing some foolish creatures from a different planet who have different freakish bodies and some freakish language, instead it looked like that something like this could've been like on earth but billions of years age. Not to forget about the incredible and true message behind this movie, which I think we all should follow because fellas we're destroying our beautiful world. I love the beautiful nature and the wildlife we still have but not the things like too much technology, racism and big luxuries. Our ancestors had something I would say a better lives then us and there had better then them but our future generations (if we continue like this) will have something worst, no nature, no tigers, no crocodiles(no wildlife), basically nothing except the damn freakish technology and laziness. I know one person cannot change the entire world but taking initiative is the first step towards achievement. We should make some more brilliant movies like these and do whatever we should to make this world a better place.

title: a unique experience on a visually fascinating fairy tale
review:
I gave to this movie a perfect 10 because it was very entertaining although it is not without it's shortcomings.

Let's break up my summary into pieces:

A unique experience because I was waiting for this movie for a really long time. In almost every sci-fi humans are the good guys with generally inferior technology. Well, not in this one.

Visually fascinating because it is, you have to see it, you just have to, trust me. The flying and "horse" riding scenes are very convincing but some of the body movement still needs some work, especially the bodies of the Omaticaya people. Another small issue is that I found a bit tiresome that on that planet everything was glowing even the grass they stepped on; this made the planet seem a bit artificial.

A fairy tale because it is a nice fable but in reality the story wouldn't end like this; and this is where my SPOILER SECTION STARTS: it would have been really hard to destroy those V-22 Osprey-like aircrafts especially because of the miniguns so this is why I'm saying that it was a nice fairy tale: the good guys won, the bad guys were punished. Yeah..., yeah..., you can tell me that I'm a negative person, but I'm telling you even if the Omaticaya won that time, the next attack will be a lot shorter, it takes only one ballistic missile with a tactical nuclear warhead to destroy their oh-so-precious tree.

title: Believe The Hype
review:
I'm sure even before you started to read this review you knew it was going to be a good one. But it's hard to find faults with James Cameron's Avatar. The fact that the movie has been in development since 1999 says a great deal about Cameron's determination and the sheer volume of work that went into producing this cinematic delight.

Avatar is a tricky one, you do actually have to pay attention and follow the plot as it happens. It's not a sit down and lounge about on the sofa movie. I'm not going to waffle on and tell you the plot though, I really don't want to ruin it for you. You can use WIkipedia or IMDb for that anyway.

The visuals in Avatar are just stunning. The CGI is literally flawless. So much so that it's not directly obvious that you're actually watching computer generated images, it all looks extremely realistic. Sam Worthington, of Terminator: Salvation fame, is absolutely brilliant in this, the same can be said for Sigourney Weaver, who features in the film quite surprisingly, as she isn't featured prominently on any of the promotional material.

There is really no reason not to watch Avatar in 3D or in an IMAX theatre, I couldn't give a completely accurate comparison of watching in 3D as opposed to 2D but the three dimensional aspect of the film worked amazingly well, people in the cinema were actually wow-ing throughout. The world of the Na'vi tribe is literally breathtaking and full of colour and life. You really do have to see it for yourself.

http://ukmore.tk/

title: The perfect dream
review:
This movie touches me emotionally in so many levels. Sullys vulnerability in real life contra his strenght in the Avatar world.

In real life his legs. His emotional vulnerability when he needs to convince Quaritch to go back into the Avatar world to enter the final stage of becoming a man. His vulnerability when he is confronted with Quaritch and Selfridge. And when he is found comatose on the floor by Neytiri. In the Avatar world when he is getting stronger in the second bow scene, and Neytiri is getting shy for the first time because she notice him as a man. At his first flight. When he makes the speech at the tree of souls. When he is standing next to his Toruk as the leader of all the clans. And in the final scene, the vulnerability of his real life body kissed by Neytiri and the power of the ending. This has got to be the best ending in movie history, both as a story, visually and regarding sound effects.

I see several themes in Avatar: 1) Dreaming and waking up. This is verbalized several times during the movie and I understand this theme much like Total Recall (1990) 2) Computer game contra real life. Avatar = representation of the gamer in a game. I think a lot of gamers recognize the perception of real life being gray at times, and perceive their real life weaknesses (physical or mental) in contrast to their physical or mental strenght in cyberspace. 3) The spiritual theme. Avatar = incarnation of god in Hinduism. That all living creatures are connected and dependent on each other. That there is a cycle of life. That you have to see others, in the sense that you have to respect them, and they have the same rights as you. That you have to learn to see for yourself, that the deeper understanding of spirituality must come from within, from yourself.

Technically Avatar is outstanding. The 3D technology is a step forward in movie history much like the dawn of sound in late 1920ies and the dawn of color in the 1920ies (bicolor) and 1930ies (tricolor). With this extra dimension in movies, future directors will be able to narrate their stories in a much more compelling and realistic way. In first person view, for instance, like in Avatar where you follow the marines out of the transport shuttle. Or, like in Avatar, enhancing the actors faces giving the impression that you can almost reach out and touch them. This effect make you look at the actors most of the time in Avator, even though the background is incredibly detailed and interesting, too. It may take a while yet though, before we see any director master the 3D as well as Cameron.

The editing of scenes and sounds in Avatar are also outstanding, with the sound from the next scene being used to end the prior scene and vice versa. Most striking is the long sequence where Sully has a voice-over while he is trained by Neytiri with inter-cutting of him being weeks older. This sequence conveys his transformation in a way that is as believable as it is moving. The use of slow motion to halt the time is outstanding. Also the use of variations of "back trunk shots" - in 3D. Finally Avatar has got to have the best moment of pure movie magic in movie history: The scene with the pure spirits landing on Sully - in breathtaking 3D.

In Wizard of Oz (1939) Dorothys first words when she enters the magnificent colored world are "I don't think we are in Kansas anymore". In Avatar (2009) when Sully wheels out of the transport shuttle we hear Quaritch voice "We are not in Kansas anymore". And then CUT to Quaritch feet in outstanding 3D. No, we are not in Kansas anymore, we are in another era and dimension of movie making. I have 700+ titles in my vote history; Avatar is my favorite.

title: Great entertainment but typical predictable and unimaginative ending
review:
Great as a fantasy special effects movie and is thoroughly enjoyable as long as you don't think. The movie goes a long way to stress how horrible aggressive, cruel and war-like humans are and then tries to portray a different, better, and more peaceful society.

So the solution to the conflict between the two cultures? Get the peaceful ones to fight and kill and feel good about it. Now how is that better or different than the humans killing to get their way?

All such anti-violence movies resolve problems by using - you guessed it - war and killing. Of course most will leave feeling the humans deserved their fate - so much for the message of needing a more caring society.

So come on Mr. Cameron and other filmmakers: For once come up with an ending that does not involve ending violence with violence. By overcoming violence through some other means (see Gandhi for example). Now that would demand real creativity, much imagination and truly thinking outside the box. Make your movie consistent with the message being portrayed rather than falling back on old warn-out clichés of peaceful folks overcoming difficulties by the violence and killing they condemn in their enemy. Add fire to fire and you get more fire. How about meeting fire with some tender compassionate water next time.

title: The movie is more than pretty
review:
I have read and heard a number of reviewers talk about how the movie is pretty, but has no story. They point out other movies that tell the same story, so what is the big deal? The big deal is how the story is told.

Walking out of Avatar, I had the same feeling I did 33 years ago when I walked out of the theater after seeing Star Wars for the first time. Someone has finally figured out how to use current technology effectively in a movie. Cameron is able to use CGI and digital 3D technology to more effectively transport the audience into a movie than I have ever experienced. While it is true I have seen and read this story elsewhere, I have never experienced it so strongly as I did with Avatar.

As to the story being 'old', as Aristotle said more than 2000 years ago there are only 7 story plot lines. How many 'new' stories are we likely to see now? And people who object that everyone already 'knows' that the actions taken by humans in the story are bad and we don't need to be reminded of it, I would suggest they ask their friends if they really did understand the extent of what humans have done to culturally 'inferior' people when encountering them before they saw Avatar. That is certainly an old story that we seem to forget often.

title: An Experience You Will Never Forget
review: Going in to see Avatar I didn't expect to see anything amazing besides the 3D effects because of the reviews of audiences who had early screenings, but after I experienced the first scene in 3D I knew that I was in for a treat. now the cost of making the 3D so real had to of been extremely expensive but well worth it. Now as far as the story goes, there is really no originality but that doesn't really matter because you'll be so amazed by the 3D you will forget all about the story. Floating mountains, amazing looking creatures, and awesome looking aliens, and breathtaking visuals, James Cameron earned his money with Avatar and will most likely win most if not all of the Oscars, but even if he doesn't we will all know that no award can justify how truly amazing Avatar really is. With spellbinding special effects, fantastic acting and an amazing score, Avatar is now the greatest Sci-fi film ever made. Even if there are more films like this, none will match Avatar's power or box office totals(over $2 Billion), but hopefully the sequels will be even better.

title: Fantastic special effects, but...
review:
Finally, as one of the seemingly few remaining human beings not to have seen Avatar yet, I had an invite to join 3 fellow film fans (two of whom had already seen the film) to visit our nearest multiplex showing the film in 3D, an invite not to be turned down.

So finally having experienced the most financially successful film of all time what was my opinion. Well, there is no denying that the special effects are quite amazing - this is a film that has to been seen in 3D, I just could not imagine it 'flat - yet as for the story line I could not help but think I had seen it all before.

During the journey home I mulled the story over in my mind and pieced it together thus - you take a little '2001 A Space Odyssey', throw in a dash of 'First Blood - Rambo', add a dollop of 'Last of the Mohecians', mix just about 'boy meets girl, boy loses girls, boy and girl get together in the end', and finally stir with a splash of almost all the recent eco-porn movies and thus you have 'Avatar'. Don't get me wrong, this does not mean the film doesn't have merit - it moves at a nice pace, the action sequences are superb, the characters display some real depth and as a whole it is very watchable, but just do not expect anything really original or totally mindblowing.

If you have not experienced this film yet do so, you will enjoy it even if only on a basic level, but I do urge you to check out the 3D version where the effects come to life, and avoid the standard version.

title: "All men are brothers, like the seas throughout the world; So why do winds and waves clash so fiercely everywhere?" Emperor Hirohito
review:
I really enjoyed this film to a certain point in the story. The visuals were amazing and obviously groundbreaking. Seeing it in 3D was kind of like having a beautifully vivid dream. I also loved the timeless message that it is our connection and inner peace that is important in living our lives. As opposed to the outer seeking that is never satisfied as personified by the corporations and military in this film. I even enjoyed the somewhat hokey way the Na'vi were portrayed as a seeming mix of Native Americans and tribal Africans...it worked.

For me it all went sour when the peaceful connected natives finally were shown the answer by the white outsider. The answer was violence. In the end the evil white power was defeated by the peaceful natives through warfare. I thought this movie might actually make it through to the end without destroying its own message, but alas it was almost obliterated. It can easily be said that the Na'vi had no choice but to fight. This might even be true, but if you want to talk about the sacredness and connectedness of all things you cannot then glorify killing without ultimately killing yourself. I would still recommend anyone seeing this movie for all the good things about it. I suppose James Cameron can't judged too harshly for creating his oh so exciting yet shallow climax. He sure does know how to bring in the money.

title: with a little more humor and better sidekicks it could be a real masterpiece
review: I won't waste your time repeating what everyone is saying about the technical aspects of this film. It's a huge technical leap for the industry and for the art of cinema too. But that's not all, it does have added value, and I disagree with most of the charges about the unoriginal story. I think it borrows from other films/stories so the viewers can get it's point using the analogies. I can't elaborate without adding spoilers, so you'll simply have to trust me. If you saw the film and you think I'm wrong I'm willing to carry the argument further using the available channels. But I have two complaints: a)not enough humor (some minor scenes with some visual gags don't count). And more importent, b) most of the characters lack character, I understand that the two major "baddies" are cartoons in nature but there's no excuse for the complete absence of personality of most of the "good" humans in the film. It's a real shame because the film came real close to perfection and a little more attention could've brought it all the way there.

title: good....but thats all
review:
It clear that the only reason people went out to see avatar is because of its ground breaking technology. The film in the visual department does not disappoint . The scenery is fantastic and the 3D is great. But there is a downside , after 30 minutes of seeing the effects , you kind of lose interest. Now and then something will "wow" you but that about it. The script does not help the film in anyway. It has only been written as a template to show off these effects and nothing else. The story is weak and been told many times before and the characters didn't connect with me. Before I watched Avatar , I heard about the story being similar to other films . I didn't mind this as films are made to be a visual experience and seeing that this is new high technology equipment that Cameron used I surely thought that would be enough to carry me through the film.

Apart from the script , there's nothing negative about the film. At the end of the day it goes down to how spectacular the film is. Cameron wanted this film to excite people and it certainly did but just not me. It seems Cameron doesn't care about using his writing abilities anymore and only thinks about the technical side of the industry which is a shame because Cameron can write amazing stories such as The Terminator's films. But you can't blame him for getting everyone out of the house to watch this film. Many people will be interested on how he did it and plus it all good for the cinema world. Should it win the best picture at the Oscars? I would say yes due to the amount of work that has been put into it and how Cameron is trying to reinvent the way we watch films.

Personally , I wouldn't call it a masterpiece. My reason being because a film that is categorised as a masterpiece has to stand the test of time. What will happen when all films uses this sort of technology? Avatar maybe the first but when everyone gets there hands on it, other films will start to outclass it. For the cinematic experience , it wasn't greater than the lord of the rings trilogy. You could feel the atmosphere , not only on the screen but all around you in the theatre. Avatar failed to capture that feeling personally.

Well Avatar is a good film , it not and will never be a classic to me. I didn't leave me with tons to say after I watched it as it wasn't that good of a film. Tell me, how long can you have a discussion on Avatar before running out of things to say? Not long I bet. Take the 3D away and it leaves you dry

title: Worth it just for the visual experience
review:
I generally judge a movie by when I look at my watch, 15 mins in (why did I bother coming), after the end (what a great movie), this was most definitely an "after the end" movie, and that is quite some feat for a 2 hour 40 min film, totally absorbed for the duration.

title: Star Wars + The Matrix + Fern Gully = Avatar
review:
Cameron created a beautiful world to get lost in. Very rewarding to take in the trees, floating mountains, and waterfalls in all their 3D splendor. I would recommend seeing it in a theater for the eye candy.

That said, Cameron really isn't good at character development and dialog. All the main players have the same kind of attitude... the army colonel, the CEO, the lead scientist, the main female native and her warrior brother... they all toss their ego about until our protagonist "proves" himself to them. Another fault is that the movie is pro-environment for some very strange reasons. It invokes a very pagan type of mentality that everything is connected, everything is one... so we don't kill more than we need to eat, we walk on trees rather than paved roads, don't set up schools, and reject medicine. But when push comes to shove and our protagonists are trying to defend the natives' way of life to the business men who want to strip mine the natural resources... they say that the natives are right, because... they have scientifically determined that all the jungle is electro-chemically networked like "synapses in the human brain". Meaning that the land has this emergent mother-goddess entity that "isn't voodoo BS... it's real." So, I'm thinking... for us here on Earth where the plants aren't one giant brain, I guess the message is that it's OK to do whatever we want.
